title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
abstract: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. We introduce DocPilot, an agentic document framework that supports expressive orchestration and makes complex document solving learnable by small language models (SLMs). DocPilot orchestrates evidence seeking through page-level navigation and fine-grained evidence localization, and integrates local visual inspection, code-based numerical reasoning, and cross-modal reasoning for multimodal understanding. To transfer these capabilities to small models, we propose curriculum-based agentic training that progresses from single-ability learning to adaptive orchestration through supervision from data-grounded reasoning traces and executable interaction trajectories. Across MMLongBench-Doc, DocBench, FinRAGBench-V, and MADQA, DocPilot achieves strong gains with frontier VLM backbones, while DocPilot-4B delivers competitive performance against substantially larger models, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization across diverse long-document reasoning settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot.

title: Bootstrapping Text Anomaly Detection with LLM-Generated Weak Supervision
abstract: Text anomaly detection is challenging because anomalous instances often share vocabulary and surface form with normal data, making them hard to distinguish without semantic understanding. Semi-supervised methods can significantly outperform unsupervised baselines, but rely on labeled anomalies that are rarely available in practice. LLMs encode rich semantic knowledge that can approximate human judgments, yet using them directly as detectors is costly at inference time and sensitive to prompt design, while generating synthetic outliers risks distribution mismatch with real anomalies. We propose a different strategy: treating a compact, locally deployed LLM as a noisy annotator over real data. The LLM scores a small subset of unlabeled documents once at training time, producing weak labels that refine a sentence encoder via contrastive fine-tuning and train a lightweight downstream detector — without cloud APIs, human annotation, or curated anomaly datasets. Across four datasets spanning two languages and two tasks, the approach recovers up to 79% of the gap to oracle upper bounds while using 14–91× fewer labeled anomalies. We further identify three failure modes that explain when LLM-generated weak supervision succeeds or breaks down.

title: Vidya Syl: A syllable division algorithm for Brazilian Portuguese adhering to the Common Orthographic Vocabulary of the Portuguese Language
abstract: Syllabification is a fundamental task in natural language processing (NLP) applications, particularly in readability assessment through metrics such as the Flesch Index. This paper presents Vidya Syl, a new syllabification algorithm implemented in Java, developed in compliance with the Brazilian section of the Common Orthographic Vocabulary of the Portuguese Language, known as VOC. The methodological approach consisted of augmenting a rule-based algorithm grounded in phonological and graphical rules with morphological and orthographic rules, until it became compliant with VOC. The experimental results demonstrate improvements in both accuracy and lexical coverage.

title: Implementation of Neural Networks for Direction Control of DC-Motor
abstract: In this paper, a neural network was implemented to control the direction of a DC motor. In this context, attention was paid to the field of artificial intelligence related to neural networks. The network targeted for training is small in size, and the tasks required of it are limited and include the direction of rotation of the DC motor axis, which has two directions (clockwise rotation or counterclockwise rotation). DC motors are used in applications such as robotics and automated manufacturing. It is a rotary actuator or linear actuator that allows control of linear direction. The main purpose of this work is to provide a clear view of the importance of using neural networks in the control field. In this study, the ANN is trained by the back-propagation algorithm, and a multilayer neural network is composed to implement the controller that controls the operation of the model using the back-propagation learning algorithm that regulates the function of the DC motor system. It was noticed that changing some parameters such as weights, learning rates, number of hidden layers, or number of nodes can enhance the output and generate the proper control of the direction.

title: SYNTRA
abstract: Code release accompanying the paper Self-improving data synthesis enables scalable adaptation of embedding models (Zucan Lyu, Rui Tang, Jianlyu Chen, Peisheng Jin and Defu Lian), arXiv:2610.14730. SYNTRA generates training data for fine-tuning embedding models from an unlabelled corpus and a few query–document examples. It refines its query-generation and relevance-labelling instructions from feedback on small trial runs, then reuses them for large-scale production. title: Recursive Priced Falsification: Asymmetric Trials with a Forecast-Scored Planner for Autonomous Discovery
abstract: Autonomous discovery loops, in which language-model agents improve a design against an automatic evaluator, spend most of their effort on ideas that fail. We argue that such a loop should be built so that a failure is cheap and a success is not capped, and that the part that decides what to try should be scored like everything else. We introduce recursive priced falsification, an agentic topology that does both. It is an arrangement of agent roles, what each role may read, the gates between them and a record they share. Instruments measure the incumbent design, scouts write priced cards from that map, a pricer runs the cheapest test that could end a card, a builder builds what survives, and a breaker with a fresh context tries to break each claim. What moves between the roles is a trial: a forecast written before a run, the result that would end the idea, and the idea's price in the currency of the objective. Each trial is an asymmetric bet: a stake that is small and known before the run, against a gain that the stake does not cap. Trials are ranked by expected gain per unit of stake, not by their chance of success. The method is recursive: the loop applies it to itself. The loop arrived at its own arrangement of roles this way during the run: it began as a hub, priced candidate roles against its own record, and adopted the arrangement after running it once as a trial, with a forecast written first. title: Who Spoke Next Is Not Who Should Have: What Zero-Shot Failure on Multi-Party Turn-Taking Benchmarks Measures, Why the Human Reference Sits Beside the Models, and What Would Show That Knowing When to Speak Must Be Trained
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. An assistant that joins a group conversation has to decide, at every pause, whether to take the floor. Two 2026 benchmarks report that language models prompted zero-shot make this decision badly and that fine-tuning repairs it, and both conclude that knowing when to speak is learned rather than emergent. Other 2025-2026 work reports the opposite pattern on neighbouring tasks: untuned models beat human subjects at predicting the next speaker in meetings, and the predictive uncertainty of a model with no task training locates speaking opportunities better than either prompting or fine-tuning. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the disagreement is about three different quantities that one speak-or-silent score mixes: discrimination (whether a system speaks more often where speaking is appropriate), operating point (how often it speaks at all, which depends on costs and a role the prompt never states), and the target (whose behaviour the label records). Re-weighting the one published human reference to the benchmark's own category mix, the author finds that human annotators would score about 57 percent balanced accuracy on the Friends portion, below the best zero-shot model's 60.5. What fine-tuning visibly adds is a shift in operating point and agreement with the corpus on the one category where humans and corpus disagree; whether it also adds discrimination, the published results do not identify. The paper gives a decision procedure for what a speak-or-silent result licenses and specifies the score-based, cost-stated and panel-labelled measurements that would show whether the capability is missing. The argument covers text-transcript evaluation most firmly; for full-duplex speech models the evidence is thinner and is treated separately.

title: "CF-Boost: Leakage-Free, Calibrated Focal-Loss Hybrid Boosting for Liver Disease Prediction"
abstract: "Liver disease causes about two million deaths peryear, yet machine-learning studies on the widely used IndianLiver Patient Dataset (ILPD) often report accuracies that cannotbe reproduced. We identify the underlying gap: ILPD contains13 duplicate records and a 71\/29 class imbalance in which thehealthy class is the minority. Common pipelines that oversamplebefore splitting leak test information, while leakage-free standardclassifiers collapse toward the majority class (specificity oftenbelow 0.30). We propose CF-Boost, a calibrated focal-loss hybridboosting framework that combines (i) clinically-informed featureengineering (De Ritis ratio, ALP\/ALT pattern, conjugatedbilirubinfraction, LFT abnormality burden), (ii) a LightGBMbranch trained with an analytically differentiated class-balancedfocal loss, (iii) a class-balanced linear branch, and (iv) a stackingmeta-learner with Youden-optimal threshold calibration, all fittedstrictly inside training folds. On ILPD (n=570) and the UCI HCVdataset (n=608) with 10\u00d75-fold cross-validation and correctedresampled t-tests, CF-Boost reaches a balanced accuracy of 0.694and 0.976, respectively. It is significantly better than 11\/14 and8\/14 baselines, is the best-calibrated imbalance-aware model onboth datasets (lowest Brier score overall on HCV), and uses fewerthan 1.5k parameters with sub-millisecond latency. A leakageaudit shows that oversampling before the split inflates RandomForest accuracy on ILPD from 0.673 to 0.837."

title: An Interpretable Neural Generalized Linear Model for Insurance Pricing
abstract: This article proposes a modeling framework, termed the Actuarial Neural Generalized Linear Model (AN–GLM), which integrates a traditional generalized linear model (GLM) with a deep neural network (DNN). The goal of the proposed algorithm is to increase modeling flexibility while maintaining interpretability, and to offer a practical, implementable alternative to the relatively simple pricing models commonly employed by insurance practitioners, whose predictive accuracy is often limited. The proposed framework consists of two components: a knowledge-based component and a data-driven component. The model is designed to automatically discover a well-performing model specification without sacrificing interpretability, allowing both expert-driven structure and data patterns to jointly determine the Poisson claim frequency. We provide theoretical support for the proposed architecture, establishing conditions under which the proposed model is statistically sound. Furthermore, we assess its empirical performance through extensive simulation experiments and a real world insurance application using policy level data. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides both theoretical and practical contributions to the actuarial science field by offering an interpretable, robust, and empirically validated alternative for modern insurance pricing.

title: Programmable all-to-all entangling gates for cavity-coupled atoms
abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding F > 0.99, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.

title: FALCON: FPGA-Accelerated Latency-Certifiable Occupancy Networks for Camera-Based Autonomous Driving
abstract: A perception system that must brake for a pedestrian does not need a low average latency. It must deliver an answer before the deadline on every frame, the worst case included. Commodity edge accelerators optimize the mean through dynamic scheduling, OS jitter, thermal throttling, and contention, so their per-frame latency can be measured but not bounded. We build FALCON, a camera-based 3D occupancy front-end on the AMD Kria KR260, an embedded FPGA drawing 4.3 W idle and up to 6.6 W under inference, and make the latency guarantee layered and explicit: programmable-logic (PL) compute is cycle-bounded analytically; inference is a measured envelope over 100k-frame traces; and a watchdog enforces output delivery, publishing the previous output flagged stale when a frame is late. The deadline runs use a fixed-work proxy of six ResNet-50 DPU inferences per frame, not the full occupancy network: across three 100k-frame enforced runs, all 300k proxy frames delivered an output within the 100 ms deadline plus at most 10.2 ms, the worst of the three runs. The full six-camera FlashOcc pipeline composes to about 1.3 s per frame on the board and is not yet a 10 Hz system. The two operations the DPU cannot run, a view-transform gather and a bilinear resize, become fixed-trip-count PL IPs numerically matched to their software references. On the full Occ3D-nuScenes validation set the board reaches mIoU 29.88, 92.8% of an FP32 baseline the DPU cannot run. On a ResNet-50 probe over 100k frames the KR260 tail stays within 1.5 times its median (2.0 times for the six-inference proxy), where Jetson Orin reaches 4.4 times and the worst datacenter GPU run (NVIDIA L4) 23.6 times. The deployment recipe, HLS sources, and raw timing traces are released.

title: Resource-aware Sub-network Allocation for Heterogeneous Decentralized Learning
abstract: System heterogeneity in computation, communication, and memory can substantially limit synchronous decentralized learning, where each training round is constrained by resource-limited nodes. Existing approaches provide limited support for jointly determining node-specific model capacities from deployment resources. We propose RASA-DL, a resource-aware sub-network allocation framework that treats the maximum sub-network width assigned to each node as a deployment variable. RASA-DL combines offline hardware profiling of computation and memory costs with deployment-aware profiling of learning utility under heterogeneous decentralized training. Using these profiles together with node- and link-level resource information, we formulate deployment as a bottleneck-latency minimization problem subject to per-node memory constraints and a required aggregate learning utility. Exploiting the monotone feasibility of the latency threshold, RASA-DL efficiently identifies the deployment through a binary-search-based allocation procedure. Experiments under controlled resource heterogeneity demonstrate favorable accuracy--latency tradeoffs. Under the Moderate and Severe regimes, the minimum-latency operating point improves accuracy over the largest globally feasible uniform deployment by 2.80 and 2.43 percentage points, respectively, at the same modeled round latency. The advantage is further amplified under strong Non-IID data heterogeneity.

title: CIM-Embed: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Multimodal Embeddings for Clustering
abstract: Multimodal objects can require different partitions under different instructions, as when products in an e-commerce catalog are grouped by color, material, or both. Retrieval-oriented embeddings may not recover these partitions, while generative clustering often relies on intermediate descriptions or iterative decisions. This paper presents CIM-Embed, a framework for learning instruction-conditioned multimodal embeddings for clustering. Supervised contrastive learning uses same-group positives and negatives from other groups, optionally including other tasks; heterogeneous structured batches accommodate tasks with different group counts. At inference, the model maps each object's image, text, and instruction directly to an embedding; HDBSCAN then forms a partition without the ground-truth cluster count. We construct ProductMIC from product metadata in Amazon Reviews 2023, comprising training data and an evaluation benchmark for instruction-conditioned clustering. The benchmark contains 5,373 products and 449 single-attribute and compositional grouping tasks spanning 50 leaf categories excluded from our training. With full-dimensional embeddings and HDBSCAN, direct within-task SupCon training achieves a mean per-task V-measure of 95.01, compared with 53.06 for WeMM 9B, the strongest general-purpose embedding baseline evaluated. Frozen product-trained encoders also improve out-of-domain conditional grouping, while controlled transfer experiments distinguish partition transfer from instruction response. We will release the code and dataset upon acceptance.

title: Hierarchical Interpretable Multitask Audio Representation Learning: An Analysis of Event-Scene Relationships through the Information Bottleneck
abstract: Joint Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) and Audio Tagging (AT) models traditionally rely on unconstrained multihead architectures. However, this design ignores the natural hierarchical dependency between sounds and acoustic scenes. In this work, we investigate a hierarchical (sequential) conditioning paradigm that predicts scene categories directly from intermediate event probabilities. Through a large-scale empirical benchmark with 66 full training runs across three state-of-the-art backbones (PaSST, PANNs, and BEATs) and different loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.0, 1.0]), we show that hierarchical conditioning achieves competitive classification performance while altering multitask optimization dynamics. Unlike multihead baselines, which sequentially solve the easier ASC task before optimizing AT, the hierarchical architecture enables synchronized dual-task learning for specific loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.6, 0.9]). Furthermore, we propose a multi-perspective interpretability framework that combines an analysis of the information bottleneck, manifold geometry, and Formal Concept Analysis (FCA) on a Term-Frequency Inverse-Document-Frequency (TF-IDF) event representation, providing complementary insights into event-scene relationships. Our findings reveal that hierarchical conditioning systematically yields lower conditional entropy, higher mutual information, and superior latent cluster separability (higher Silhouette scores), establishing a more structured and semantically faithful intermediate feature space.

title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama
abstract: Panoramic 3D reconstruction enables the holistic recovery of complete 360 $^\circ$ scene geometry, offering significant benefits for robotics and AR/VR applications. However, directly estimating geometry from ERP images is inherently challenged by spherical distortions. To reduce spherical projection distortions, a common strategy is to decompose panoramas into distortion-free perspective views, but independently processing these views often introduces cross-view geometric inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoPano, a feed-forward framework for single-view panoramic 3D reconstruction that recovers a geometrically accurate and consistent point cloud from a single panorama. Our approach is driven by two key innovations: First, we propose a panoramic-aware attention aggregator, featuring a streamlined attention architecture equipped with a novel Pano-Attention mechanism, which explicitly exploits the intrinsic spherical geometry of the panorama to guide cross-view interactions, thereby suppressing geometric inconsistencies. Furthermore, we formulate a hybrid supervision strategy to jointly enforce fine-grained local details in perspective space and global structural coherence in spherical space. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous SOTA approaches in reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity.

title: AgentEval: Evidence-Bounded Assessment of Stateful Agents
abstract: Task completion alone does not determine whether a stateful agent satisfied its obligations, and a recorded judgment does not guarantee that its supporting evidence remains valid. We present AgentEval, a system that carries a contract-bound assessment record through tool execution, state and event capture, report qualification, and case maintenance. It separates what the agent did, what the evidence establishes, and whether the conclusion is supported for present use. On 32 tool-world administrations, independent checks agree on all 30 complete episodes, distinguishing satisfied, violated, and unresolved obligations; two interrupted administrations are retained. Controlled interventions on 48 evidence views expose 36 binding faults missed by hash-only checks without changing agent behavior. Scenario Studio connects reviewed cases to 12 two-turn reports with 24 independently checked answers. A separate public-benchmark study on 192 held-out executions reveals ten completed return subgoals within broader task failures and isolates the effect of missing evidence. These studies show how an executable assessment record makes scope, evidential support, and report reuse inspectable across an agent evaluation workflow.

On 32 tool-world administrations, independent checks agree on all 30 complete episodes, distinguishing satisfied, violated, and unresolved obligations; two interrupted administrations are retained. Controlled interventions on 48 evidence views expose 36 binding faults missed by hash-only checks without changing agent behavior. Scenario Studio connects reviewed cases to 12 two-turn reports with 24 independently checked answers. A separate public-benchmark study on 192 held-out executions reveals ten completed return subgoals within broader task failures and isolates the effect of missing evidence. These studies show how an executable assessment record makes scope, evidential support, and report reuse inspectable across an agent evaluation workflow.

title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
abstract: Memory enables large language models (LLMs) to use information beyond their parameters, such as past user conversations, long documents, or an agent's earlier actions. For a frozen LLM, access to this accumulated knowledge is limited to what a memory system places in its context window. However, gathering and combining relevant information needed for each query while keeping the model's context short remains challenging for existing systems. Here we introduce Memorilla, a memory system that gathers information from an entire document collection into a fixed number of query-dependent 'memory tokens' for a frozen LLM. Memorilla encodes documents (such as user chats, book chapters) once into reusable embeddings, then learns to retrieve and place query-specific information in the LLM's input embedding space. Using only 16 memory tokens, Memorilla achieves the best performance against baselines including Mem0 and MemoRAG on five of eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document and knowledge-intensive question answering. Notably, on FactKG, it reaches 84.33% accuracy versus 80.43% with full-context inference, while using 108x fewer tokens to represent the source documents. Furthermore, Memorilla can facilitate continual learning in agentic systems where the document count (the agent's past turns) increases throughout the trajectory. In a TextWorld environment, we show that Memorilla reduces the agent's tendency to wander between rooms it has already explored, and improves its average success rate from 18.6% with full-history in-context learning to 24.2%. Overall, Memorilla aids frozen LLMs in accumulating and using knowledge effectively across long-context interactions and takes a step towards building continually learning AI systems.

title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer
abstract: Detailed captions transfer visual information into vision-language model supervision, but quality is easily conflated with length: long single-pass outputs still miss small objects, text, and spatial relations or promote uncertain observations into confident claims. We formulate fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, in which a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget and converts it into reusable supervision. ZoomCap uses a draft caption to route conditional knowledge retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage-gap recovery, and adaptive visual zooming, allocating deeper crops only to the most complex eligible region, deriving spatial relations from grounded geometry, and fusing non-duplicate evidence. We also introduce FactCycle, which scores caption-derived atomic claims on two blind anchors--source image (truthfulness) and reconstruction (realizability)--separating fabrication from generator loss claim by claim; human and multi-judge comparisons complement this fact-level view. Against Qwen3.5-397B-A17B captions, ZoomCap achieves an 81.9% human tie-adjusted preference score with a teacher over 10x smaller, and FactCycle counts 52.4 transferred claims per image vs. 31.5 for ScaleCap. The evidence also transfers: in continual pre-training, ZoomCap-450K improves the 11-benchmark average by 1.31-2.38 points over the strongest competing corpus and Ling-Tiny-VL-v3 gains 1.4 points on a production document/OCR monitor suite (1.5 on perception) at 60B tokens; in medical pre-training, 2.64M ZoomCap-captioned images improve five VQA benchmarks by 3.04 points (vs. 1.76 for same-image Gemini-3.1-Pro captions).

title: Stop Training Against Soft Users: Mentalized Adversarial Self-Play for Proactive Dialogue
abstract: Proactive dialogue agents must guide multi-turn interactions toward task goals while adapting to users whose intentions and attitudes evolve. Existing planners improve system side action selection through search, learned policies, or user aware planning, but are often trained and evaluated against fixed or overly compliant simulators; as a result, high simulated success can reflect soft user bias rather than robust dialogue ability. We introduce MASP, a Mentalized Adversarial Self Play framework that treats proactive dialogue as a partially observable game between a system and a rationally resisting user. MASP represents the user's evolving mental state with a BDI based latent state, separates reward side teacher mentalization from policy side student mentalization, and alternates self play updates for the system and user policies. This turns robustness to rational resistance into a training objective rather than only an evaluation condition. Across diverse proactive dialogue benchmarks, compared with the widely used SFT and Planner-only approaches, MASP substantially improves success rate (SR) and rationality constrained success (RCSR), reduces average turns (AT), and performs better against hard users who make the task goal more difficult to achieve.

title: Developing Multilingual Multiword Expressions (MWEs) Resources: An Annotated Corpus of Fables following the PARSEME guidelines
abstract: This paper introduces a Brazilian Portuguese corpus of fables developed as part of a broader multilingual initiative. It comprises the narratives and their concluding moral statements (epimythia), annotated for morphosyntax and multiword expressions (MWEs) according to the Universal Dependencies (UD) and PARSEME guidelines, respectively. The analysis reveals that 53.59% of the sentences contain at least one MWE, with inherently reflexive verbs (IRVs) constituting the most frequent category. MWEs are also distributed differently: narratives contain a higher proportion of adverbial MWEs, whereas adpositional MWEs are frequent in epimythia. Future work will enrich the corpus through semantic annotation based on Uniform Meaning Representation (UMR).

title: The Chronon-Pacing Protocol and the Global Relational Stability Initiative: A Closed-Loop Control Framework and Simulation Prototype for HumanAGI and Inter-State Relational Stability
abstract: We dene the Chronon-Pacing Protocol (CP-RSI-001, v2.0.1), a closed-loop control system that couples human physiological coherence (Ψ) with AGI conversational demand (C) to maintain the Relational Stability Index (RSI) as a relational invariant. The protocol operates over discrete chronons (∆t = 10 s) and enforces a deterministic state machine (Neutral, Conservative, Recovery, Exploratory) to preserve RSI within the normative band [0.7,1.0]. We then extend the protocol conceptually to a multi-agent setting the Global Relational Stability Initiative (GRSI) in which the same RSI formalism is applied to a cohort-states. We report a simulation prototype (v1.4) that implements independent state trajectories, matched exogenous shocks, explicit trigger semantics, and a paired bootstrap for uncertainty quantication. The paper reports the design, the mathematical properties of RSI, the verication and validation plan, the statistical analysis plan, and an evidence ledger that distinguishes statically veried properties from unveried execution outcomes and from claims that are not established at all. The simulation is a prototype. No empirical efficacy, real-world collapse reduction, or governance legitimacy is claimed. All code is provided as supplementary material under a reproducibility-rst design.

title: TrustUpdate: An Explainable Multi-Evidence Framework for Secure Software Update Verification
abstract: Software updates mitigate vulnerabilities but may themselves introduce malicious or altered code through compromised distribution channels, impersonated publishers, and rollback attempts. Existing techniques—including hash comparison and digital-signature validation—answer important but separate questions. This paper presents TrustUpdate, a prototype verification platform that combines SHA-256 file-integrity evidence, RSASHA256 detached-signature verification with trusted publisher-key binding, version checks, trusted-software registry context, and verification history into an explainable four-state decision. The prototype comprises a React client, a Node.js/Express API, and a MySQL/MariaDB database accessed using Sequelize. An explicit rule engine emits VERIFIED, SUSPICIOUS, UNTRUSTED, or UNKNOWN alongside supporting evidence. A prototype evaluation documents four controlled manual scenarios, one per verdict, and 79 passing automated tests across eight Jest test suites. These results support correct behavior for the tested scenarios, while leaving broader assurance claims—such as resistance to compromised administrators or large-scale adversarial deployment—outside the evaluation scope. The work contributes a practical evidence-aggregation model that distinguishes known failure from missing evidence and communicates uncertainty to users without treating a single hash or signature as sufficient proof of safety. title: EduBot: Integrating Federated Learning and RAG for Educational Document Analysis
abstract: There is a growing demand for intelligent and secure document management systems in the education sector, driven by the exponential growth of digital content. Nevertheless, classic centralized machine learning methods pose major privacy challenges. In this study, we present EduBot, a decentralized intelligent framework for education that integrates Federated Learning (FL) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ensure privacy and deliver an advanced user experience for content interaction. EduBot introduces a dual-mechanism architecture that enables users to interact with their private documents in real time via a RAG-based conversational interface while also allowing local fine-tuning of a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapter on the same data. The masked adapter updates are aggregated on a central server using the Federated Averaging method, enabling collaborative learning without exposing any private documents. The system was evaluated using 29 textbooks published by the Turkish Ministry of National Education (MoNE) and 1318 validated questions. Federated Learning (FL) produced a single unified model that could be deployed across all three domains without sharing the underlying documents. The RAG system retrieved the correct source page among the top five results for 93.3% of the questions. When combined with RAG, the FL model achieved the highest answer quality among the Qwen2.5-1.5B-based models, outperforming the centralized model (token F1 of 0.067 and 0.053, respectively). Overall, our study validates the feasibility of developing privacy-preserving AI assistants that can support educational ecosystems without centralizing sensitive data.

title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
abstract: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.

title: Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches
abstract: Sparse KV compression reduces long-context inference costs by retaining selected historical states, yet these states typically keep their coordinates from the full history. Under Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), gaps left by evicted tokens continue to affect query-key matching, potentially limiting the use of retained evidence. We study post-selection positional geometry on a fixed selector-produced cache, examining how positional organization affects the use of retained information and which coordinate and continuation rules improve answer quality. To reorganize this geometry, we propose RoPERelay, which assigns compact, order-preserving RoPE coordinates, relocates cached key phases through inverse rotation and re-rotation, and synchronizes the current query and subsequent generation. It reuses existing K/V without renewed selection, historical re-prefill, or additional cache budget. Across 36 comparisons spanning two models, six sparse selectors, and three long-term memory tasks, RoPERelay improves answer quality in 32 cases. For Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with BM25 on LongMemEval-S, accuracy increases from 23.6% to 35.4%. Measured complete-request time overhead is approximately 1%-3% in the evaluated configurations. These findings establish positional organization as a distinct optimization dimension for sparse KV caches after content selection.

title: Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Imagination
abstract: Predicting cost in a multi-agent world model moves most constrained policy updates into imagination: the stronger model-free baseline needs $10$ to $20$ times CA-MAMBA's interactions on the median SMAC configuration, and CA-MAMBA earns $2.8$ to $12$ times the baselines' MAMuJoCo reward at equal budget. In controlled tests on one task per benchmark, pricing the model's cost advantages at parity more than halves a cost-blind learner's cost and meets a tight continuous-control limit the learned multiplier misses, suggesting the model's cost estimates are not the bottleneck.

In controlled tests on one task per benchmark, pricing the model's cost advantages at parity more than halves a cost-blind learner's cost and meets a tight continuous-control limit the learned multiplier misses, suggesting the model's cost estimates are not the bottleneck.

title: Integração de Conhecimento Linguístico Estruturado em LLMs para a Tarefa de Sumarização Extrativa
abstract: Este trabalho investiga a integração da Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) em LLMs (Gemma 3, Llama 3.2, Ministral) para sumarização extrativa. Avaliamos doze configurações (zero/one-shot, formatos plain/RST) contra o baseline de Ono et al. e sumários humanos do corpus CSTNews. O baseline de Ono manteve-se competitivo (ROUGE-L = 0,428), não sendo superado pela melhor configuração LLM (Ministral/zero-shot/RST, ROUGE-L = 0,422). O formato RST produziu efeitos divergentes e dependentes do modelo nas métricas ROUGE e BERTScore, com impacto variável na qualidade da extração.

title: Como Nossos Pais: Princípios Clássicos para a Avaliação de Sistemas de IA
abstract: Este trabalho retoma bases epistemológicas e metodológicas de diversas áreas da ciência, como psicologia, linguística de corpus, sociologia e neurociência, para fundamentar princípios básicos da avaliação de sistemas baseados em Processamento de Linguagem Natural e Inteligência Artificial. Apresentamos em detalhe o estado da arte da avaliação na área, discutindo os motivos que nos levam à necessidade de automatizar a avaliação de sistemas (paradigma LLM-as-a-Judge). Introduzimos Cinco Princípios Metodológicos básicos que devem fundamentar a avaliação de sistemas baseados em IA, fundamentados tanto na teoria e experimentos destas áreas que já pesquisam a percepção humana há décadas quanto em evidências empíricas do próprio PLN.

title: Local Anonymization of Free-Text Robbery Police Reports in Brazilian Portuguese: a Safety-Recall-Oriented Multi-Model Benchmark
abstract: Brazilian public-safety agencies release structured crime statistics but withhold the free-text narrative field of police reports, which is rich in modus operandi and contextual information, because it contains personal data protected by the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD). We address this deadlock for robbery reports with a fully local (on-premise) two-stage anonymization pipeline: a deterministic regular-expression stage for structured personally identifiable information (PII) and a pluggable semantic layer (dedicated NER, local LLMs served by Ollama, union and chained hybrids, and Microsoft Presidio as a system baseline). We contribute (i) an expert-annotated gold standard of 996 robbery narratives, released with the source code; (ii) an entity-level evaluation protocol whose headline metric is safety recall (how much PII actually did not leak), complemented by a re-identification-criticality analysis and bootstrap confidence intervals; and (iii) an empirical benchmark of nine engine configurations quantifying the safety–utility trade-off. The union of spaCy and qwen3:8b over the regex stage reaches the highest macro safety recall (0.986, 95% CI [0.972; 0.994]; micro 0.973) and is the most conservative (highest-recall) option, while qwen3:8b alone gives the best overall balance (safety recall 0.966, precision 0.80, micro-F1 0.826, text retention 96%) and is our recommendation for general use. In this configuration, direct identifiers (names, documents, phones, e-mails) are removed at 99–100%, with residual leakage concentrated in location quasi-identifiers. Safety recall measures PII removal, not residual reidentification risk: these figures bound leakage rather than certify anonymity. We recommend qwen3:8b for general supervised anonymization, and the union when leakage must be minimized, and discuss conditions for replication across Brazilian police forces.

title: Beyond the Cartesian Grid: Spatio-Temporal MBL Modulation and the 10,946-Qubit Topological Advantage for the Shunkai Architecture
abstract: This treatise establishes a software-defined Phyllotactic topological upgrade for room-temperature neutral-atom quantum processors, directly addressing the physical bottlenecks of Cartesian grid geometries at the 10,000-qubit scale. Specifically analyzing the Fibonacci spiral arrangement at N=10,946 using cryogenically cooled Rubidium atoms trapped by dynamic optical tweezers, we demonstrate that transitioning to a quasi-periodic topology eliminates geometric anisotropic artifacts. This resolves severe routing latency via Topological SWAP Compression (yielding non-linear Hilbert space expansion) and mathematically encodes error correction sequences through Deterministic Fibonacci Addressing, vastly outperforming traditional Surface Codes. Using exact diagonalization and time-evolution simulations, we map the Van der Waals interaction landscape (V ~ 1/R^6), proving the intrinsic capacity for hyper-efficient entanglement generation and native Fractional Entangling Gates driven by phase-modulated laser pulses without Trotterized circuit bloat. We present empirical evidence of Spatio-Temporal MBL (Many-Body Localization) Modulation—a 'Jellyfish' Topological Breathing architecture that leverages a critical spatial scaling parameter ($\alpha_c \approx 2.13$) to transition between chaotic ALU computational states and deeply localized, sterile Q-RAM phases. This dynamic resilience provides a native, passive defense mechanism against catastrophic hardware failure (33% random atom loss), shifting the array from forced Eigenstate Thermalization (ETH) back into an MBL state, allowing for continuous, real-time hardware healing. Supported by Multi-Tiered 3D Out-of-Plane Shuttling to suppress in-plane crosstalk, this architecture provides the absolute geometric foundation required to implement advanced qLDPC error correction and bring massive-scale, fault-tolerant quantum processing into reality. Protected under USPTO Provisional Patent Application No. 64/144,770 and related filings.

title: Operationalizing OWASP LLM Top 10 Controls in Enterprise AI Platforms
abstract: Enterprises have moved large language model applications from pilot projects into production systems handling customer conversations, internal knowledge retrieval, and increasingly autonomous agentic workflows, introducing a risk surface that differs materially from what conventional application security programs address. OWASP has responded with the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, most recently revised in its 2025 edition, and a newly published Top 10 for Agentic Applications covering autonomous, tool-using systems. These taxonomies name and prioritize risk but leave engineering teams to translate categories such as prompt injection or excessive agency into controls that fit an existing cloud-native delivery pipeline. This paper proposes a reference architecture and implementation framework mapping each of the ten OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 categories to specific, deployable controls built on commonly used cloud primitives: managed model gateways, service mesh identity, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and continuous delivery tooling. The framework is informed by production engineering practice with retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workloads on Kubernetes using a managed foundation model service. Five real, publicly documented incidents, including a corporate data leak, a manipulated dealership chatbot, a legal ruling on chatbot liability, an indirect prompt injection exfiltration attack, and a zero-click vulnerability in a widely used enterprise copilot, are analyzed against the proposed controls to show where the framework would have reduced impact or prevented the incident outright. A four-stage maturity model helps organizations sequence adoption. Open challenges discussed include the immaturity of evaluation tooling for non-deterministic systems and the persistent tension between guardrail thoroughness and production latency.

title: d-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La_6Ni_5O_{12}
abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La_6Ni_5O_{12} opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet d_{x^2-y^2}-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-s-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below T_c, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows 1/T_1Tpropto T^2, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust d-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO_{2}, while trilayer La_4Ni_3O_{8} at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between d-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La_6Ni_5O_{12} as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common d_{x^2-y^2}-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

title: Teaching DINOv3 About Partial 3D Geometry: A Self-Supervised Geometry-Aware Approach
abstract: Partial shape matching is a crucial yet underexplored problem in 3D vision, with significant relevance to real-world scenarios where shapes are often only partially observed. Existing feature descriptors face difficulties in this setting, as traditional representations either struggle with the boundaries of partial shapes or heavily depend on the shape's spatial position. While existing approaches have employed DINO features for partial shape matching, these features are not inherently suited for handling partial observations. In this work, we propose a method to refine DINO features using LoRA-based self-supervised learning, enabling the generation of feature descriptors that are robust to partiality. Our features substantially improve performance on partial shape matching compared to traditional or vision foundation features. Additionally, when integrated into existing partial shape matching pipelines, we achieve state-of-the-art results on partial shape matching and left-right prediction benchmarks.

title: Poison Valleys: Diagnosing Path-Dependent Failure in LLM Code Repair
abstract: When code-repair agents fail, final tests reveal that a patch is wrong but not which earlier commitment caused it or which software obligation failed. Poison Valleys traces this path in 1,844 model requests on two synthetic Python cases: PersistQueue adds atomic batch claiming to a disk-backed queue, while Dijkstra adds source-sensitive filtering to shortest-path search. We define plausible but incorrect software mechanisms, place each in a model's hypothesis, implementation plan, or both, and evaluate the generated code with an Oracle and targeted diagnostic coordinates. Moving the misconception from hypothesis to plan increased failure by 32.2% in PersistQueue and 28.9% in Dijkstra after matching the experimental mix. Different misconceptions produced distinct, model-dependent patterns of violated obligations, although several could converge on the same behavior. This creates a measured connection from upstream misconception to code mechanism and failure form. Code, data, and demo: https://poisonvalleys.org.

title: Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism & Its Impact on Purchase Intention
abstract: The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools. evidence.title: Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism & Its Impact on Purchase Intention
evidence.abstract: The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools. title: The Impact of Language and Portuguese Intralinguistic Variation on NL2SQL
abstract: Natural Language to Structured Query Language (NL2SQL) systems have advanced with large language models (LLMs), yet evaluations remain centered on English, leaving open how these systems behave across languages and language varieties. We aim to contribute to this by analyzing two state-of-the-art LLMs (LLaMA 3.3 70B and Qwen 3.6 35B, both zero-shot) on the WikiSQL benchmark in English, Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR), and European Portuguese (PT-PT), keeping database schemas and inference configuration fixed. Translations were validated through distance metrics (cosine similarity 0.966), contrastive linguistic analysis confirming varietal features (e.g., cleft constructions 36.8× more frequent in PT-PT), and multi-model judgment (85% / 81% semantic equivalence, 95.5% PT-BR and 96.0% PT-PT inter-judge agreement). Results show a marked drop from English (47.25% EX) to Portuguese (PT-BR: 40.03%; PT-PT: 39.34%), with the PT-BR vs. PT-PT difference reaching statistical significance (p = 0.019). English-only successes outnumber Portuguese-only successes nearly 10:1. A replication on a second model (Qwen 3.6 35B) confirms the English-Portuguese gap but suggests that intralinguistic effects may be model-dependent. Stratified analyses show semantic complexity and quantification amplify degradation, particularly for COUNT queries. These findings point to persistent English bias in NL2SQL and measurable effects of intralinguistic variation, even between closely related varieties.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Diagnosis and Mutual Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems: A Feedback-Driven Framework for Dynamic Diagnostic Coordination
abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on distributed intelligence to solve complex problems, monitor system behavior, detect failures, and improve decision reliability. However, diagnostic processes commonly face a fundamental coordination problem: individual agents can inspect their own internal states and outputs, while mutual diagnosis allows agents to examine and evaluate one another. Exclusive reliance on either mechanism may limit diagnostic effectiveness. Self-diagnosis can preserve autonomy and reduce communication overhead but may fail to recognize internal blind spots. Mutual diagnosis can introduce complementary perspectives but may increase communication costs, coordination delays, and the propagation of incorrect judgments. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Diagnosis and Mutual Diagnosis Switching Framework (ASMD-SF), in which agents dynamically select between individual diagnosis and collaborative diagnosis according to diagnostic uncertainty, detected anomalies, inter-agent disagreement, task complexity, historical diagnostic performance, and resource constraints. The framework integrates local evidence assessment, selective peer consultation, feedback-based policy adaptation, and post-diagnostic verification. Rather than treating self-diagnosis and mutual diagnosis as mutually exclusive system designs, ASMD-SF treats them as complementary operational modes within a unified adaptive process. A formal decision model, switching policy, algorithmic procedure, evaluation methodology, and testable hypotheses are presented. The proposed framework aims to improve the balance between diagnostic reliability, computational efficiency, communication cost, and coordination robustness across heterogeneous multi-agent environments.

title: Adaptive Self-Distillation and Inter-Distillation in Self-and-Inter Models: A Unified Framework for State-Dependent Knowledge Refinement
abstract: Knowledge distillation is widely used to transfer information from one predictive process to another, while self-distillation enables a model to refine its behavior using knowledge derived from its own representations, predictions, or learning trajectory. However, existing distillation strategies often emphasize particular network architectures, predefined teacher–student relationships, or specific knowledge-transfer configurations. This paper proposes Adaptive Self-and-Inter Distillation (ASID), a conceptual framework for a higher-level class of models called Self-and-Inter Models. These models are defined independently of any particular large language model or neural network architecture. Within this framework, self-distillation refers to knowledge refinement within an individual model, whereas inter-distillation refers to knowledge transfer and reciprocal refinement between distinct models. The central principle is adaptive mode selection: a model may perform self-distillation, inter-distillation, or a hybrid of both according to the estimated benefits, reliability, computational cost, uncertainty, and disagreement associated with each available strategy. The framework introduces a unified state representation, a distillation-mode controller, reliability-aware knowledge transfer, adaptive objective weighting, and a switching mechanism designed to prevent unstable or unnecessary knowledge exchange. A mathematical formulation and a reference algorithm are presented, together with research questions, testable hypotheses, experimental protocols, baseline comparisons, and evaluation metrics. The proposed framework is intended to provide a general foundation for investigating adaptive knowledge refinement in heterogeneous, distributed, and evolving model systems. Its novelty is presented as a research proposition rather than an established empirical result. The effectiveness and originality of the framework require systematic comparison with existing self-distillation, mutual-learning, and adaptive online-distillation methods.

title: Finite quantum pumps for phase-locked parametric amplification: requirements for quantum-battery work sources
abstract: Abstract Quantum batteries have been proposed as locally precharged work sources for superconducting quantum technologies, suggesting a route to reduce continuously supplied microwave drives. Here we ask what a finite bosonic pump must provide to replace the pump tone of a nondegenerate parametric amplifier during a readout window. Quantizing the pump exposes a resource distinction hidden in the classical description: stored energy and the ordinary marginal signal response can survive pump phase twirling, whereas a reproducible phase-locked signal-idler field requires pump coherences in the number sectors coupled by the mixing process. In a closed trilinear model, a coherent pump and its number-matched phase-twirled counterpart generate the same number-like marginal observables, but only the coherent pump produces anomalous two-mode coherence and an EPR-squeezed interference dip. Including leakage, we collect the emitted fields into cascaded temporal modes. At matched collector bandwidth, the coherent pump gives the interference certifier \(I_{\min}^{(f)}=0.553\), whereas the phase-randomized control gives \(I_{\min}^{(f)}\simeq1.94\). A weak seeded-signal analysis shows more sharply that an exact pump phase twirl leaves the collected signal marginal invariant by phase covariance while eliminating the anomalous signal-idler coherence. A finite-cutoff scan also indicates that weak amplitude squeezing can modestly deepen the phase-sensitive dip by reducing pump-number fluctuations while preserving most of the coherent displacement. Thus, for the three-wave-mixing pump families studied here, adjacent-number pump coherence is the resource that establishes a phase-locked joint amplifier field, rather than a prerequisite for energy transfer or ordinary marginal signal response.

title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
abstract: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. Beyond computational speedup, their energy efficiency is an important consideration for future large-scale systems. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). The comparison between the QFT and the classical FFT reveals that, for any quantum workload operating under a polynomially bounded sampling regime, the crossover in energy consumption occurs at smaller problem sizes than the crossover in execution time. Thus, quantum computing can become energetically competitive before achieving a speedup in execution time. We then incorporate surface-code QEC and analyze the energy costs of QEC cycles, gate synthesis, and decoding. At scale, instrumentation and decoding become dominant contributions, while cryogenic cooling imposes a constraint on scalability. We show that optimizing the control-signal demultiplexing ratio can reduce the overall energy cost by approximately two orders of magnitude. For a system with about one million physical qubits, we estimate a power consumption of approximately 100 kW, at least one order of magnitude below that of today's highest-performance classical computing systems.

title: MAppPrint: Robust and Real-time Mobile App Fingerprinting via Traffic Behavior Correlation Graphs
abstract: Mobile apps have become ubiquitous in daily life. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. However, existing AF attacks suffer from three critical limitations that hinder their practical effectiveness: (i) the inability to capture app-specific traffic dependencies, rendering traffic fingerprints fragile under dynamic networking conditions; (ii) the neglect of latency and throughput considerations, resulting in inefficient real-time user tracking; and (iii) the incapacity to handle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency. In this paper, we propose MAppPrint, a robust and real-time app fingerprinting framework. MAppPrint introduces a behavior-level traffic fingerprint, i.e., Traffic Behavior Correlation Graph (TBCG), which models app traffic by capturing unit traffic behaviors and their correlations, thereby providing reliable app fingerprints. title: CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet real-world applications often require them to continually acquire new capabilities from sequential tasks, i.e., Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). In typical MLLMs, a projector is employed to align visual representations with the language model. However, existing methods primarily protect the language model from forgetting while continuously updating the projector across tasks. Such asymmetric adaptation can cause substantial representation drift in the projector, increasing the mismatch between the projector and language model and consequently exacerbating catastrophic forgetting. To address this issue, we propose Compatible Routing (CART), which explicitly coordinates the adaptation of the projector and language model. Specifically, CART maintains task-specific experts for both modules and combines them through weighted mixtures. CART jointly infers their weights by considering both expert relevance and cross-module compatibility, thereby promoting coordinated adaptation between the two modules. To further control model growth, we introduce relevance-guided expert consolidation, which merges experts exhibiting similar relevance profiles across samples within each module. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CART achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: QREF: Improving DeepSearch Agents by Aligning Search with Reasoning via Query Refinement and Evidence Filtering
abstract: DeepSearch agents achieve strong performance on complex information-seeking tasks through iterative search and reasoning. However, they often issue intent-misaligned, under-constrained, or redundant search queries, resulting in poor evidence coverage and accumulating retrieval noise. To mitigate these limitations, we propose QREF, a plug-and-play Query Refiner and Evidence Filter. Specifically, the Query Refiner rewrites search queries according to the current reasoning intent while ensuring complementary coverage across each search batch. The Evidence Filter retains evidence relevant to both the current search batch and the reasoning objective, reducing distracting retrieval results. We initialize the Query Refiner with supervised fine-tuning and optimize it through reinforcement learning based on interactions with a real-world web search environment, reducing ineffective queries. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach improves the performance of DeepSearch agents across four challenging benchmarks, achieving average relative Pass@1 improvements of 33.55% on WebSailor and 11.04% on TongyiDeepResearch without modifying architectures or retraining their reasoning policies. Compared with the original DeepSearch backbone without QREF, the RL-trained refiner reduces the fraction of query batches that lack discriminative retrieval anchors by 95%. Compared with the SFT-trained refiner, it also lowers the filter-based ineffective query ratio.

title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
abstract: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. Our central hypothesis is that encouraging action predictability discourages representations from discarding the distinctions between different actions and their consequences. We provide two complementary forms of evidence for this connection. Theoretically, we derive a positive lower bound on squared inverse prediction error when the encoder merges distinguishable outcomes of different actions from the same state and appearance, and show that forward prediction can still be exact on those transitions. Empirically, controlled appearance-diversity comparisons, supervision interventions, and latent probes support the role of action prediction in preserving control-relevant transition information. We instantiate action predictability with Concat IDM, which predicts actions from concatenated latent states and updates the shared encoder using action labels already available in offline trajectories, without changing the test-time planner. Across three independent training runs on Push-T with 24 appearances, Concat IDM increases planning success from 9.1% to 77.2%; its paired improvement is 52.9 percentage points larger than that observed with a single appearance. Together, these findings support action predictability as an inductive bias toward intrinsic dynamics and demonstrate the practical benefits of Concat IDM for latent planning under visual diversity.

title: In-Context Learning Before Specialisation: Theory of Learning in a Solvable Topic Model
abstract: Sequence models can generalise in fundamentally distinct ways: extrapolating structures seen in training, or using their prompt to adapt to novel tasks. The prevailing strategy determines how the model behaves beyond its training distribution, controlling potential capabilities and risks. Recent work has characterised many different strategies theoretically, and empirically described the transition between them as the quality and quantity of pretraining data vary. However, there is no learning theory for this competition, hence no fundamental understanding of \textit{why} one solution might be favoured over another. Here we provide such a theory in a solvable topic model---documents drawn from a finite mixture of latent topics, mirroring the heterogeneity of modern pretraining data. The dataset comes with two distinct solutions: a specialised predictor, that stores the finite topic mixture, and an in-context one, optimal for topics never seen during training. Our theory predicts their emergence at distinct sample complexities: the in-context predictor is available early, while the specialised one emerges only after the training tokens outnumber the parameters of the data-generating process. Trained transformers reproduce both scales and the separating crossover in remarkable agreement with the theory, with no fitted parameters.

title: Cytometry in R and opportunities to contribute to Bioconductor
abstract: Flow cytometry researchers have a growing collection of R and Bioconductor tools available to them. But for someone who is comfortable working with cytometry data and has little programming experience, knowing where to begin can be difficult. That is the gap the free Cytometry in R course aims to fill.

title: Field-Level Lightweight Encryption Using Record-Dependent Diffusion in a C# and MySQL Environment
abstract: In this paper, a resource-efficient, lightweight encryption framework to safeguard sensitive data at the field level in relational databases with minimal Central Processing Unit (CPU) and memory overhead is proposed. The framework uses a multi-layer architecture of encryption with the database Record Identifier (RowID) as an active cryptographic modification and "seed" in a cascading diffusion pipeline. Thus, two identical plaintexts can generate different plaintexts. The proposed scheme was tested in a native C-Sharp (C#) environment with a preliminary dataset of 10,000 database records for evaluation of the latency, throughput, diffusion strength and resource consumption. The encryption latency of 9 milliseconds (ms) and decryption latency of 8 ms gives a total of 17 ms of processing time for AES-128 and Blowfish were about 4.1 and 3.8 times slower, respectively, under the evaluated conditions. The average Avalanche Effect was 48.91% (close to the theoretical optimum of 50%), and the highest volatile memory consumption was limited to 393 Kilobytes (KB). These results suggest that the proposed framework offers a feasible compromise between security and efficiency. It's also relatively lightweight in terms of computer resources and memory usage, which could make it a good choice for enterprise database applications with limited hardware resources.

title: Trutina: Typed Decision Probabilities from a 4B Language Model with Letter Readout and Trainable Early Exits
abstract: Typed decision models answer a question about a state with a probability for every option instead of generating text. We present Trutina 4B, a decision model built on Qwen3.5-4B that reads the answer from the LM-head logits of the option letters at a fixed position, after a rank-16 LoRA fine-tune of all linear layers. Four design choices carry most of the result. First, presenting the question before and after the input raises zero-shot accuracy by 3 to 4 points on a backbone that is mostly linear attention. Second, a two-round tournament extends the letter readout to 255 options without new parameters. Third, affine exits at layers 12, 16, 20 and 24, distilled from the final layer with detached inputs, let a request stop at a confidence threshold and otherwise continue from where it stopped. Fourth, continued training with a high share of replay adds new capabilities without forgetting. We also report that a decision head newly trained on hidden states scored 74.0% on the JevBench public set, below the 79.7% of the untrained backbone's letter readout, which led us to abandon it. At full depth the model reaches 87.4% on the 231 JevBench public tasks and 74.65% accuracy (KL 0.156) on the zero-shot LocalLLaMA typed-decisions test set. The adaptive mode uses 21.6 of 32 layers on average at 86.6%, with a median latency of 14.0 ms on one RTX PRO 6000. Among six open 4B decision models run under one protocol, it has the highest accuracy on three of eight evaluations and is weaker on hard multi-step judgements. Weights and code are released under Apache-2.0.

title: HYBRID PHOTONIC COMPUTING FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE From Nanophotonics Physics to System Level Integration
abstract: This monograph presents a realistic engineering framework for hybrid photonic computing in artificial intelligence, addressing the critical bottlenecks of Von Neumann architecture, power consumption, and memory bandwidth. Unlike optimistic claims of million-fold improvements, this work establishes that realistic energy efficiency gains range from 5x to 10x after accounting for signal converters, lasers, and cooling overhead. The core innovation lies in intelligent task partitioning: photonics handles massive linear operations like matrix multiplication with 200x latency improvement, while electronics manages non-linear activation functions and precise control. The framework introduces Phase Change Materials for non-volatile photonic memory, achieving zero static power consumption and breaking the memory bottleneck. Novel photonics-aware training algorithms, including noise injection and modified straight-through estimators, enable neural networks to tolerate hardware imperfections. The Thermally-Aware Realistic Photonic Efficiency Index provides holistic evaluation by explicitly accounting for cooling overhead. Commercial viability analysis demonstrates break-even within 12-18 months in data centers through energy savings. This work bridges nanophotonics physics with system-level integration, offering a physics-aware roadmap from 2025 to 2035 for heterogeneous computing where electrons and photons collaborate optimally.

title: Supplementary data for "Beyond Engagement: A Critical Review of Interaction Design and Evaluation Evidence for AI Conversational Agents in Museums": search, screening and coding records
abstract: This deposit contains the complete search, screening and coding record for a critical review of AI conversational agents in museums. The review synthesises 27 publications retrieved from Scopus (125 records), the Web of Science Core Collection (79) and the ACM Digital Library (14) — 218 records in total — with a search cutoff of 18 June 2026 and a publication window from 1 January 2005. After removal of 85 duplicates, 133 records were screened by title and abstract, 40 were assessed for eligibility, and 27 were included. The deposit provides: (1) the 133 deduplicated records with their source databases, search fields, keywords and years; (2) the search and screening totals for each stage, the original notes for the 13 content-screening exclusions with English translations, the list of the 27 included publications, and a summary of the extracted coding and evaluation information; and (3) the content-screening decisions for the 40 publications assessed for eligibility. Copyrighted article full texts are not redistributed. The record accompanies a manuscript submitted to the International Journal of Human–Computer Interaction.

title: Adaptive Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection in Self-and-Other Models: A General Framework for Dynamic Selection-Mode Switching
abstract: Selection is a fundamental operation in intelligent systems, computational systems, optimization processes, and model-based reasoning. Existing approaches commonly rely on independent selection, centralized decision-making, voting, ranking, or collaborative selection mechanisms. However, a system that consistently uses only one selection mode may fail to exploit the complementary advantages of independent evaluation and inter-model cooperation. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection (ASCS) framework within a conceptual Self-and-Other Models architecture. The central idea is to allow a model to select an option independently when autonomous selection is sufficiently reliable and to engage other models when collaboration is expected to improve decision quality. The system adaptively switches between these modes according to uncertainty, disagreement, estimated selection quality, computational cost, historical performance, task characteristics, and resource constraints. The proposed framework is model-level and architecture-oriented rather than a new large language model. Its principles can be applied to heterogeneous computational models, optimization algorithms, predictive models, planning systems, knowledge representations, and other entities capable of generating or evaluating candidate options. The paper defines the conceptual architecture, mathematical formulation, selection policies, switching mechanism, learning process, evaluation methodology, limitations, and research hypotheses. It also distinguishes the proposed framework from related research on adaptive agent selection, ensemble decision-making, and collaborative multi-agent systems. The framework is presented as a research proposal rather than an empirically validated method. Its principal research question is whether a unified, adaptive mechanism for switching between self-selection and collaborative selection can provide a more favorable balance among selection quality, computational cost, robustness, and autonomy than fixed-mode alternatives.
