title: Analisis Sentimen dan Pemodelan Topik Ulasan Pengguna terhadap Kepercayaan, Kualitas Layanan Elektronik, Keadilan Harga, dan Pengalaman Pelanggan pada Aplikasi Maxim di Google Play Store
abstract: The increasingly competitive ride-hailing industry in Indonesia highlights the need to understand user perceptions through application reviews. This study aims to analyze sentiment and identify dominant topics in Maxim user reviews on Google Play Store related to trust, e-service quality, price fairness, and customer experience, and to examine the relationship between sentiment and user ratings across these aspects. A quantitative text mining approach was applied to 539,645 raw reviews collected through web scraping. From the most recent 24-month period, 4,985 reviews were selected using proportional stratified sampling. The analysis involved text preprocessing, aspect-based theme extraction, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for topic modeling, sentiment classification using Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Pearson correlation testing. Sentiment labels were assigned using manual anatomi. The results show that customer experience was the most dominant theme (59.5%), with 74.0% positive sentiment, while e-service quality had the highest proportion of negative sentiment (32.8%). The SVM model achieved an accuracy of 93.78%, compared with 76.53% for Naïve Bayes. All four aspects showed significant positive correlations between sentiment and user ratings (r = 0.466–0.653; p < 0.001), with customer experience exhibiting the strongest correlation. These findings provide empirical insights into user perceptions of digital transportation services through review-based text analysis and offer practical input for prioritizing service improvements, particularly in e-service quality.

These findings provide empirical insights into user perceptions of digital transportation services through review-based text analysis and offer practical input for prioritizing service improvements, particularly in e-service quality.

title: Cross-Embodiment Causal Transfer from Human Videos to Robot Manipulation
abstract: Scaling robot manipulation models requires large amounts of interaction data, yet collecting diverse real-robot experience remains costly. Human manipulation videos, in contrast, provide abundant and diverse task experience that could potentially benefit robot learning. However, differences in morphology, action spaces, and control mechanisms make human motions unsuitable as direct supervision for robot actions, raising a scientific question: what knowledge in human videos should be transferred across embodiments to robot manipulation? To address this question, we analyze subtask transfer through the lens of causal beams, focusing on which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies should be retained to support local task effects. Based on this perspective, we propose Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST). CBST learns manipulation-related representations from human videos and grounds them in task-level semantic variables using robot demonstrations. Within a predefined manipulation model, causal-beam constraints guide contextual information selection by requiring retained assignments to sustain local mechanism outputs while preserving nontrivial responsiveness to retained inputs. The selected semantic information conditions a world-action model, allowing the robot to generate actions from its own observations without requiring human-robot motion correspondence. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show improvements in task success over the corresponding world-action model baselines.

title: Realization Divergence in Multi-Provider Quantum Computing: A Pre-Registered Study of What Survives Measurement
abstract: Quantum programs pass through compilers, transpilers and vendor services before execution. However, the distance between what was written and what runs is rarely measured. We call this distance realization divergence: the observable difference in how an identical source circuit is realized and behaves across quantum software stacks. We report a hardware study across three vendors and four devices, combining pre-registered predictions with explicitly identified exploratory analyses and amendments. In a compilation experiment with assigned placement policies, embedding radius correlates with two-qubit overhead at Spearman 0.805, against 0.492 for circuit size. Under a fixed lowest-index policy, an eight-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani circuit exhibits greater execution divergence than a twelve-qubit circuit on IQM Emerald. The opposite ordering occurs on IQM Garnet. Both comparisons replicate across two repetitions with disjoint confidence intervals. These results support a placement-dependent explanation, without isolating individual hardware noise mechanisms. The same ordering inversion is absent on the all-to-all IonQ control. On Rigetti Cepheus, a follow-up using topology-aware native placement found no consistent advantage in correct-answer probability for either submission track, but did not establish equivalence between the tracks. Structural comparisons depend on metric weighting, placement and device generation. Provider interfaces also limit observability: Rigetti's supported-operation list remained unchanged across a device generation that replaced the native entangler. We classify silent interface failures in composed toolchains and identify checks at toolchain boundaries, connecting valid cross-provider comparisons with concrete software-quality practices.

title: Decomposing Brain-LLM Alignment with Interpretable Semantic Representations
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) predict neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension, but the linguistic information underlying this brain alignment remains difficult to interpret. We use SCRIBE, an interpretable contextual semantic representation spanning 65 neurocognitively grounded semantic properties, as a lens for decomposing the brain alignment of one LLM, LLaMA2-7B. Using variance partitioning between LLaMA2-7B and SCRIBE on naturalistic fMRI data from seven participants listening to narrative stories (Moth Radio Hour), we separate brain-predictive variance shared between the two representations from variance unique to each. We find that shared variance is the dominant component across the whole brain and language-related regions, while both representations also retain significant unique contributions. We then examine whether the concreteness of individual semantic properties relates to shared and SCRIBE-unique brain-predictive variance. Concrete properties show greater shared variance with LLaMA2-7B than abstract properties across the whole brain and most examined regions, whereas abstract properties do not show greater SCRIBE-unique variance. Finally, property ablations reveal that semantic contributions extend across multiple dimensions, with cumulative effects on both shared and SCRIBE-unique variance. Together, these results show that, for LLaMA2-7B on this dataset, a substantial portion of brain-LLM alignment is associated with interpretable semantic information, while revealing complementary brain-predictive semantic information beyond the LLaMA2-7B representation.

title: Hybrid Generative-Tagging Decoding for Efficient Product Attribute-Value Extraction
abstract: Attribute-value extraction is important for building high-quality product catalogs in e-commerce. Existing systems either rely on generative or tagging strategies for extracting the attribute names and their corresponding values. Tagging models directly label spans in the source, making them fast and grounded, but they cannot produce values that require reformatting or generate rare attribute names outside their label space. Generative models avoid these drawbacks by generating both attribute names and values token by token, but this auto-regressive nature makes them slow and limits attribute coverage. We introduce hybrid generative-tagging decoding, a novel model architecture that combines tagging source spans and open-ended generation. For frequent attributes whose values are copyable, a tagging head extracts values directly from the source. This lets the generative head focus on the remainder - rare attributes outside the tagger's label space and non-copyable values, including implicit or normalized values. Integrated into vLLM inference, the hybrid decoder raises attribute coverage by 10% and extracts 63% more correct attribute-value pairs at no precision cost, while reducing latency by 44%.

title: A retrospective systematic study on hierarchical sparse query transformer-assisted ultrasound screening for early hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), ranking as the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, demands urgent improvements in early detection to enhance patient survival. While ultrasound remains the preferred screening modality due to its cost-effectiveness and real-time capabilities, its sensitivity (59%–78%) heavily relies on radiologists’ expertise, leading to inconsistent diagnostic outcomes and operational inefficiencies. This study introduces the Hierarchical Sparse Query Transformer (HSQformer), a novel hybrid architecture that synergizes Convolutional Neural Networks’ (CNNs’) local feature extraction with Vision Transformers’ (ViTs’) global contextual awareness through latent space representation and sparse learning. Unlike prior approaches that often require complex structural modifications or sophisticated design techniques, HSQformer dynamically activates experts via a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework, achieving hierarchical feature integration without structural redundancy. Evaluated across three clinical scenarios: single-center, multi-center, and high-risk patient cohorts, HSQformer outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) models and matches senior radiologists’ diagnostic accuracy while significantly surpassing junior counterparts. These results demonstrate HSQformer’s potential to standardize HCC screening, reduce human expertise dependency, and improve early diagnosis rates. The full code is available at https://github.com/Asunatan/HSQformer .

title: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
abstract: Classical simulation of magic state factories, including distillation, cultivation, and code switching, is challenging because of their substantial non-Clifford content. We introduce $\texttt{magna}$ (magic-state-factory assessment via global network algebra), a classical simulator that simulates such protocols as cheaply as Clifford circuits. $\texttt{magna}$ expresses the figures of merit of a protocol, namely the acceptance rate and the fidelity of the accepted states, as tensor networks, which it reduces globally by exploiting a structural correspondence with transversal gates on quantum codes. $\texttt{magna}$ further supports feedforward conditioned on arbitrary functions of mid-circuit measurement outcomes, including decoder outputs. We simulate Bravyi--Haah distillation with up to 100 output magic states at a cost that does not grow exponentially in the number of outputs, and achieve state-of-the-art sampling times for distance-5 magic state cultivation on both color codes and RP$^2$ surface codes. Finally, we validate nonlinear feedforward on a logical-level distillation protocol with 15 rounds of decoder-dependent feedforward. $\texttt{magna}$ aims to contribute to the key infrastructure for the large-scale evaluation and optimization of magic state factories.

title: Debates about the IT work of the future at Faculty of Exact Sciences, UNICEN
abstract: El presente trabajo sistematiza los debates surgidos en la jornada organizada por la Facultad de Ciencias Exactas (UNICEN), donde especialistas de diversos sectores de la comunidad informática analizaron las transformaciones derivadas del auge de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA). Los disertantes trataron los impactos de las nuevas tecnologías en el trabajo informático, los nuevos perfiles y nuevas posibilidades que se abren a partir de ello, los impactos en la formación y las nuevas demandas educativas, las cuestiones éticas que aparecen cómo corolario de su uso, y el impacto que tienen estas tecnologías en la soberanía nacional. En el presente trabajo se desarrollan los puntos tratados en la disertación, y se elaboran algunas reflexiones alrededor de esas temáticas, con el foco puesto en la necesidad de que los espacios de encuentro y diálogo conduzcan a un consenso de planificación para el desarrollo nacional de una industria estratégica de gran importancia.

title: Beyond Toxicity: Evaluating Language Models for Ableism Detection in Online Social Media
abstract: Ableism is a form of discrimination directed at people with disabilities that can appear through explicit offenses, but also through subtle, indirect, and context-dependent expressions that are difficult to identify automatically. This challenge remains underexplored in content moderation, particularly in Brazilian Portuguese. This paper investigates how different levels of prompt information affect the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in detecting ableist comments on social media. To this end, we build a dataset from YouTube comments related to disability-related content, followed by manual annotation. Four LLMs are evaluated using five progressively detailed prompts, ranging from a simple classification instruction to prompts that include definitions, examples, contextual information, and the video transcript. Results show that more informative prompts tend to improve classification performance, although the effect varies across models. Qualitative inspection further reveals that LLMs often struggle to distinguish ableist discourse from criticism of ableism, as well as to separate ableism from other forms of offensive or discriminatory language. These findings highlight the importance of contextualized prompting for sensitive classification tasks and point to the need for further research on ableism detection in Portuguese.

title: PathRounds: a pathologist-in-the-loop review harness built as a Claude artifact
abstract: PathRounds is a review harness for pathology AI: a single-file review page (crop decisions, yes/no checks with editable lines, exhaustive fields marked blind to the model, tissue drawing and grading) that runs as a Claude artifact, in a browser, or behind a self-hosted standard-library server; and a Python package that builds review rounds with known sampling designs (stratified audit with inclusion probabilities, active learning, exhaustive fields, adjudication of discordances) and estimates precision, recall and cell-level sensitivity with Horvitz-Thompson estimators and bootstrap confidence intervals.

title: Benchmark data: effect of compact data types (byte/short vs int) on procedural maze generation time in Unity
abstract: Measurements for the article "Optimization of procedural maze generation in Unity" (Venhlovska Y., Marchuk G., Liubchenko D.; Visnyk of Lviv Polytechnic National University, Series: Information Systems and Networks, submitted 2026). The study evaluates how replacing int fields with the more compact byte and short types in the maze cell class affects maze generation time in Unity 6000.4.3f1 (C#, Mono). Seven algorithms (Aldous–Broder, Binary Tree, Depth-First Search, Hunt-and-Kill, Kruskal, Recursive Division, Sidewinder) were run on five maze sizes from 5×5 to 100×100, 100 runs per configuration, before and after optimization (7,000 measurements). Files: two CSV files with the measurements — maze size, generation algorithm, generation time, path search algorithm and path search time (original benchmark logs with an added header row); the description of the experimental environment; an Excel workbook with the statistical analysis (descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney test with Holm correction, Cliff's delta, bootstrap confidence intervals, model fit, memory estimate). See README.md for column descriptions.

title: Adaptive Reasoning and Collaborative Reasoning between Self-and-Interaction Models within a World-Model Architecture: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Mode Switching
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental states, dynamics, and potential future outcomes, supporting prediction, planning, and decision-making. However, a general architectural question remains: how should a system organize its reasoning process when independent reasoning and collaborative reasoning offer different benefits under changing conditions? Independent reasoning can reduce communication overhead, preserve model autonomy, and enable efficient local inference. Collaborative reasoning can improve coverage, expose disagreements, combine complementary representations, and support the resolution of complex or uncertain situations. Neither mode is universally optimal. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for adaptive reasoning and collaborative reasoning between Self-and-Interaction Models within a World-Model architecture. The framework distinguishes three architectural components: a world model representing environmental dynamics, self-models maintaining internally organized representations and reasoning processes, and interaction models representing relationships, information exchange, and coordination among self-models. A mode-selection mechanism determines whether reasoning should proceed through an individual self-model, through coordinated interaction among multiple models, or through a hybrid process combining both modes. Mode selection is formulated as a sequential decision problem involving expected reasoning quality, uncertainty, computational cost, communication overhead, model disagreement, and the consequences of error. The framework does not assume that the underlying models are large language models, nor does it require a fixed multi-agent implementation. It can be instantiated using symbolic models, probabilistic models, learned dynamics models, model-based control systems, or heterogeneous computational components. This paper defines the architecture, formalizes the switching mechanism, describes a reasoning lifecycle, and develops propositions and an experimental protocol for future validation. Its central hypothesis is that reasoning performance may improve when the system selects its reasoning mode according to task conditions rather than relying permanently on independent reasoning or permanent collaboration. The proposed framework is a conceptual research contribution, and its comparative advantages remain to be established empirically.

title: SEMANTIC ANALYSIS OF UZBEK LANGUAGE TEXTS USING THE INCEPTION PLATFORM
abstract: This article examines the application of the INCEpTION platform to the semantic analysis of Uzbek-language texts, emphasizing linguistic annotation, knowledge representation, and the development of computational language resources. INCEpTION is a web-based semantic annotation platform that supports collaborative annotation, knowledge-assisted labeling, and machine-learning-assisted annotation workflows. The study investigates how its functionalities can be adapted to the linguistic characteristics of Uzbek, an agglutinative Turkic language with extensive morphological variation and relatively flexible word order. Particular attention is given to named entity recognition, semantic relation annotation, word sense disambiguation, and the identification of context-dependent meanings. The research adopts a descriptive and comparative methodological approach based on established studies in natural language processing, semantic annotation, and computational linguistics. The article proposes an annotation framework for Uzbek texts and identifies methodological challenges associated with morphological complexity, contextual ambiguity, annotation consistency, and limited annotated resources. The findings indicate that INCEpTION provides a technically suitable environment for organizing human-supervised semantic annotation projects, although its effectiveness for Uzbek depends on the availability of appropriate linguistic guidelines, annotated datasets, and compatible language-processing models. The study contributes to the methodological foundations of Uzbek natural language processing and outlines practical directions for developing semantically annotated Uzbek corpora.

Particular attention is given to named entity recognition, semantic relation annotation, word sense disambiguation, and the identification of context-dependent meanings. The research adopts a descriptive and comparative methodological approach based on established studies in natural language processing, semantic annotation, and computational linguistics. The article proposes an annotation framework for Uzbek texts and identifies methodological challenges associated with morphological complexity, contextual ambiguity, annotation consistency, and limited annotated resources. The findings indicate that INCEpTION provides a technically suitable environment for organizing human-supervised semantic annotation projects, although its effectiveness for Uzbek depends on the availability of appropriate linguistic guidelines, annotated datasets, and compatible language-processing models. The study contributes to the methodological foundations of Uzbek natural language processing and outlines practical directions for developing semantically annotated Uzbek corpora.

title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.

title: Optimal First-Order Methods for a Class of Structured Hölder-Smooth Problems
abstract: Convex optimization with Hölder-continuous gradients has attracted considerable attention as a framework bridging smooth and nonsmooth optimization. For this class, Nesterov's universal fast gradient method attains the optimal black-box complexity, and we study whether exploiting further problem structure can further improve this bound. In this paper, we study an important class of Hölder-smooth problems, namely regularized $\ell_p$ regression with $p\in(1,2)$, whose loss has a $(p-1)$-Hölder-continuous gradient and for which the universal method requires $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2/(3p-2)})$ iterations. title: FilterFusion: Prior-Guided Adaptive Filter Fusion for Efficient Video Denoising
abstract: Real-world video denoising for communication systems must handle mixed degradations such as sensor noise, compression artifacts, and motion-induced inconsistency while remaining deployable under tight latency budgets. Purely deep models often achieve high accuracy but come with significant computational cost, whereas classical filters are robust and efficient but insufficiently adaptive. We present FilterFusion, a prior-guided multi-frame denoising framework that combines temporally-aware learned features with an interpretable bank of denoising branches. The model predicts a low-cost guidance signal and uses it to adaptively mix a compact set of denoising responses at the original resolution. The lightweight design uses only 109K parameters and explicitly injects temporal variance and spatial variance cues into the low-resolution controller. On CRVD (real sensor noise), it reaches 34.72 dB PSNR and 0.9330 SSIM with only 0.18 GFLOPs (network-only). Because the filter-bank operations are simple and regular (Gaussian blur, median, weighted sum), a straightforward compiled C implementation of the synthesis path achieves 17.9ms per frame (55.9 FPS) on a single CPU thread at 1080p---exceeding real-time and 122--252 times faster than lightweight CNN baselines that require over 2 seconds per frame. The results demonstrate a strong quality-efficiency-speed trade-off and a practical route to real-time denoising through low-resolution control and explicit filter-based synthesis.

title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
abstract: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

title: ReviewPilot: A Multi-Agent System for Screening and Data Extraction in Systematic Reviews
abstract: Systematic literature reviews follow the PRISMA process of screening scholarly works and extracting evidence from included studies. Deep research tools based on large language models (LLMs) can search and summarize the literature but do not record which studies are excluded or where extracted values come from. We develop a conversational multi-agent system called ReviewPilot that automates the PRISMA workflow from paper screening to information extraction. Researchers can tailor criteria and schemas through dialogue, and a project memory keeps their configurations and revisions. Each screening decision comes with its reason and each extracted value with its source. On epidemiological expert reviews, ReviewPilot outperforms a single-prompt LLM and AgentSLR across three LLMs, with screening macro F1 up to 0.776 and extraction F1 up to 0.788. Case studies in biomedicine and human-computer interaction show close agreement with human annotators, suggesting that ReviewPilot can transfer beyond epidemiology. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhaoqianXue/ReviewPilot.

title: When Judges Agree and Are Wrong: Consistency-Accuracy Dissociation as a Blind Spot for Label-Free Evaluation
abstract: Label-free evaluation methods, such as self-consistency filtering, majority-vote aggregation, and agreement-based reliability scoring, rely on an implicit assumption that consistency can serve as a proxy for correctness when ground-truth labels are unavailable or expensive to obtain. In this paper, we test this assumption directly. Using four financial QA datasets (multiple-choice and free-form), ten consistency dimensions, and two frontier model families, we measure the joint distribution of consistency and accuracy at the level of individual examples rather than in aggregate. We find that 60% of all incorrect answers fall in the high-consistency region (consistency $\geq$ 0.8), and that 77.7% of these show complete answer collapse, i.e. identical wrong answers across all perturbation variants. This high-consistency/incorrect quadrant cannot be detected by any evaluation signal that is built on agreement alone, as the model appears maximally reliable while being wrong. We show that the phenomenon is robust to the choice of consistency threshold t (it persists from t=0.50 to t=1.00), is shared across model families, and is concentrated in specific intersections of perturbation dimension and domain. We map where this quadrant occurs, analyze its stability properties, and discuss the implications for evaluation pipelines that use agreement-based signals in place of human labels.

title: PM-USHA International Conference Series – जञनसत (Jñānasetu): The Bridge of KnowledgeARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE FUTURE OF COMMERCE
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming an important force in the transformation of contemporary commerce. Its applications now extend across marketing, retail, e-commerce, customer service, forecasting, decision support, supply chain management, and business operations. This paper examines the role of AI in shaping the future of commerce by synthesising existing academic literature on AI-enabled commercial transformation. The study adopts a conceptual and descriptive approach based on a narrative review of peer-reviewed secondary literature. The review focuses on five interrelated themes: personalisation and consumer engagement, predictive decision-making, intelligent automation, AI-mediated customer experience, and responsible AI governance. The synthesis indicates that AI is shifting commerce from standardised to increasingly personalised interactions, from reactive to predictive decision-making, and from predominantly manual processes towards human-AI collaboration. These developments can improve efficiency, relevance, convenience, innovation, and competitiveness. At the same time, expanded use of consumer data and algorithmic decision-making creates significant concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accountability, consumer autonomy, and workforce transformation. The paper argues that technological capability alone is insufficient to create sustainable commercial value. The future of commerce is likely to depend on the ability of organisations to combine AI capabilities with human judgement, consumer trust, ethical governance, and sustainability considerations. A conceptual framework is proposed in which AI-enabled capabilities influence commerce transformation and commercial outcomes, while responsible governance acts as a critical enabling condition. The paper concludes that competitive advantage in an AI-enabled economy will depend not merely on the speed of AI adoption, but on how effectively and responsibly organisations integrate AI into commercial systems and stakeholder relationships.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Tourism
abstract: In an era of rapidly evolving tourism, staying ahead of emerging trends is paramount. Tourists’ travel habits are continuously adapting to these new trends, which include digitalisation, responsible and sustainable tourism, and a surge in domestic tourism. For the tourism sector, swiftly adjusting and responding to these new realities is crucial for regional sustainability. Amongst these trends, AI is a transformative force reshaping tourism. Integrating big data and AI technologies has been identified as a disruptive phenomenon, warranting a thorough understanding of their current and future roles within the industry. AI’s capabilities extend beyond simple conveniences; it can recommend cost-effective flights, suggest accommodations, and offer comprehensive support to travellers. Recent studies highlight that AI-driven personalisation enhances tourist experiences by tailoring services to individual preferences. As the tourism industry embraces these technological advancements, it becomes crucial to consider the implications for sustainability, ethical considerations, and the human touch in tourism and hospitality. This chapter provides a comprehensive exploration of the future of AI in the tourism industry. By examining topics such as the delineation of the tourism industry, the role of AI in the tourism landscape, and presenting a futuristic view, this chapter will offer valuable insights into how AI is set to revolutionise tourism.

title: Adaptive Self-Knowledge and Cross-Model Knowledge Integration for World Models: A Unified Framework for Selective Internal Consolidation and Inter-Model Knowledge Exchange
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental states and dynamics that support prediction, simulation, and decision-making. However, knowledge integration within world-model systems presents a fundamental architectural question: should new information be consolidated within an individual model, or should knowledge be exchanged and integrated across multiple models? Persistent internal integration may preserve model autonomy and reduce communication overhead, whereas cross-model integration may exploit complementary knowledge and resolve uncertainty that cannot be addressed by a single model. Neither mode is universally optimal across tasks, environmental conditions, and stages of learning. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Knowledge and Cross-Model Knowledge Integration framework for world models. The framework distinguishes self-knowledge integration, in which an individual world model consolidates its own observations, memories, latent representations, learned dynamics, and predictive errors, from cross-model knowledge integration, in which multiple world models exchange and reconcile compatible, complementary, or conflicting knowledge. A meta-level controller estimates the expected utility of each integration mode and adaptively selects internal consolidation, inter-model exchange, or a hybrid operation according to uncertainty, knowledge novelty, model disagreement, expected information gain, computational cost, communication cost, and integration risk. The framework is model-agnostic and does not require large language models. It can be implemented using learned latent dynamics, predictive state representations, probabilistic models, structured memories, or other computational mechanisms suitable for world modeling. This paper formalizes the architecture, defines its optimization objective and switching procedure, proposes safeguards against negative knowledge transfer, and develops an empirical evaluation protocol. The central research proposition is that adaptive selection between internal and cross-model knowledge integration may offer a more favorable balance among predictive accuracy, knowledge retention, adaptability, and resource consumption than systems that permanently rely on only one integration mode. This proposition remains to be tested experimentally.

title: BDA supplementary derivations for BDA-BOUNDARY-DEFENSE-002
abstract: This supplement records five additional target paradigms for the Boundary Defense Agent (BDA-BOUNDARY-DEFENSE-002): Common Lisp, Brainfuck, spreadsheet formulas, an Analytical Engine-style program, and AWK. It is separate from the canonical BDA package and its Non-Normative Tests (NNT) companion. The supplement Manifest names and hashes the canonical BDA package Manifest as its parent artifact. The BDA Specification, Conformance Tests, and Semantic Index define the rules and acceptance criteria. Integrity. Boundary_Defense_Agent_Supplement.zip, 22 files, SHA-256 9b6faaf8bf15e03ce7bd33c6ea41037dcaa986bdb195fe61403aa4be8211f46d. Supplement Manifest (BDA_Supplement_Manifest.json), SHA-256 7219be84eb87656340946592d067df0911aa151d1803b9f4f28e738a1994e3ac; its parent is the BDA package Manifest, manifest_ref 76aa2959343a8efd8242b38d306b31952040a6650094d1669f9de7d242aa52f0. The BDA package is archived as a separate record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23384976. Use of AI tools. The author designed and calibrated the harnesses of the derivations in this supplement. Large language models were used openly, as tools to accelerate research and production, with manual review: they produced the renderings (Common Lisp, Brainfuck, spreadsheet formulas, an Analytical Engine-style program and AWK) and the comparators (the Rust rendering and the reference output spec_192.txt) in an AI-provider environment, as the study artifacts reported in Section 6 of the article; they are not reference implementations. No tool is an author; the author is accountable for the content. What matters is not which tools touched the files but whether they can be verified: the supplement has its own Manifest, which names the pack Manifest as its parent.

title: AI-Driven Personalization and Transparency Effects on Customer Experience and Engagement
abstract: Customer experience (CX) is transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) to create value through AI advancement, with the collaboration of people for personalization and transparent interactions across the digital journey to gain a competitive advantage. This chapter creates premises that integrate and resolve contradictions in research on how CX creates value by using AI. Six literature fields were identified by a systematic review of articles that address how AI enables CX and value in the long term. To establish the research traditions by comparing the key concepts and metatheoretical assumptions addressed by each literature field, two concepts arise from analysis: customer experience and value emerge through AI advancement and adoption without human assistance, or it emerges through Human-AI collaboration. Identifying the alignment using a metatheoretical lens by research traditions forms four premises. These premises help to develop concepts about how experience creates value in the AI-driven world by explaining its framework and developing ideas for the future

title: Attacks During Training and Secret Backdoors in Systems That Detect Network Intrusions
abstract: Deep learning has transformed Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) from static rule-based tools into adaptive classifiers that learn complex patterns from packet, flow, and telemetry data. While this improves the detection of emerging threats, it also expands the attack surface of the NIDS itself. Beyond runtime evasion, attackers can target the training process through noisy labels, data poisoning, targeted poisoning, backdoor insertion, and continuous-learning exploitation. These attacks can alter model behavior before deployment, creating hidden weaknesses while maintaining normal validation accuracy. For example, poisoned data can shift decision boundaries, and backdoor triggers can cause malicious traffic to be classified as benign. Therefore, securing deep learning-based NIDS requires protecting the entire machine learning pipeline This chapter presents a taxonomy of training-time attacks, examines their impact on model behavior, summarizes defensive controls across pipeline stages, and highlights future research challenges.

title: A Novel Perspective on Explainability: Measuring and Tuning XAI Consensus
abstract: Neural networks are commonly regarded as black boxes, necessitating post-hoc Explainable AI (XAI) methods. However, different feature attribution techniques applied to the same model and data often yield divergent explanations, undermining the reliability of any single method. This work proposes a model-centric approach that moves beyond evaluating individual XAI methods, focusing instead on optimizing neural network architectures toward cross-method consensus via surrogate-based multi-objective hyperparameter tuning. Cross-method XAI consensus, defined as the degree to which diverse attribution techniques yield convergent explanations for a given architecture, is formalized as a novel optimization objective. Consensus is operationalized by aggregating local attributions into global feature importance profiles, standardizing them, and quantifying convergence via the Euclidean distance. This score is integrated as a second objective alongside predictive loss into a Kriging-based Bayesian optimization framework using desirability functions. Empirical evaluation across 14 diverse datasets confirms that explicitly tuning for explainability is feasible. The framework reveals a prevalent performance-explainability trade-off in most in-distribution settings, while analysis of tuning trajectories and selected architectures reveals exploitable structure in the hyperparameter-to-consensus landscape. These findings introduce cross-method XAI consensus as a practical, model-level criterion for neural architecture selection and provide a quantitative basis for analyzing the performance-explainability trade-off.

title: MedPAO-VL: Interpretable and Protocol-Compliant Agent for Structured Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Despite the remarkable generalization capabilities of Large Language Models, generating clinically accurate and structured radiology reports from medical images remains a significant challenge. Current end-to-end approaches function as black boxes, prone to factual hallucinations and generating ungrounded findings. This lack of reliability and failure to adhere to domain-specific structuring protocols, fundamentally limits their clinical utility. We present MedPAO-VL, a multimodal agent that shifts the paradigm from monolithic generation to explainable, iterative, protocol-compliant structured report generation. Unlike deterministic models, our plan-act-observe loop functions as a goal-oriented agent: it first perceives the Chest X-Ray through an explainable vision module designed to capture inherent diagnostic uncertainty, then iteratively refines the generated report by observing semantic discrepancies and self-correcting its generation for better alignment with visually detected clinical findings. Evaluation of our framework demonstrates that this agentic reasoning improves clinical correctness and completeness, achieving an expert-rated accuracy score of 3.5/5 and a structural score of 4.3/5. By prioritizing pathology specific explainability and iterative refinement over opaque end-to-end mapping, MedPAO-VL offers a transparent and clinically viable alternative for automated structured radiology report generation.

title: ISW-Agent: Integrating LLM-Driven Dialogue with n8n Workflow for Internal Solitary Wave Remote Sensing Image Processing
abstract: Internal solitary wave (ISW) remote sensing requires task parameters and spatial information to be transferred across image acquisition, detection, stripe extraction, and propagation prediction. Here, we present ISW-Agent, which integrates large language model (LLM) interpretation with n8n workflows and independent scientific models through structured task constraints, geospatial transformations, and stage-specific output validation. In tests of 120 Chinese instructions per backend, GPT-5.6 Sol and DeepSeek both achieved a strict task-match rate of 94.2%, with all intents and execution decisions matching the reference. Sentinel-1 cases demonstrated continuous processing from dialogue requests to wavefront prediction for the specified scene. Of 50 timed scenes, 39 completed detection, extraction, and prediction with a median turnaround time of 48.04 s; 11 stopped after empty extraction. Across 3,408 controlled fault-injection runs, retries recovered 234 transient-failure conditions and output validation rejected 234 structural defects, while 61 provenance or completeness errors indicated the need for content-consistency checks. Overall, ISW-Agent thus connects natural-language requests to traceable spatial processing chains for multimodel ISW analysis.

title: RoboCloth: A Large-Scale Real Cloth Material Dataset for Neural Reflectance Reconstruction
abstract: We present RoboCloth, a dataset of 500 real cloth materials captured under flexible, calibrated camera and lighting configurations, where both are robotically controlled during acquisition. Each material is imaged in approximately 580 high-dynamic range frames spanning a wide view-light hemisphere; camera poses are refined via structure-from-motion and aligned to the robot frame, yielding per-material sparse surface geometry and structured per-point reflectance observations ready for neural material training. We demonstrate the value of this data through a two-stage neural reconstruction pipeline: Stage 1 trains a shared MLP decoder on our corpus to learn cloth material priors; Stage 2 then freezes the decoder and fits a dense 2048x2048 latent texture to each target material. Evaluating on held-out materials from our own dataset and on the independent UBO2014 benchmark, we show that a decoder trained on our captures outperforms decoders trained on existing measured reflectance datasets and analytic PBR fitting, transferring to unseen acquisition systems without modification. The dataset, calibration files, observation tensors, and train/test splits are released under CC BY 4.0 on the Hugging Face Hub.

title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
abstract: Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning. Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins. Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network (HTN). The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask. Results propagate upward under \textbf{AND} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task. On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2.45 and 4.69 percentage points, respectively.

title: Structured Metadata Filtering as a Semantic Search Refinement Strategy in RAG Systems for the Legal Domain
abstract: La Generación Aumentada por Recuperación (RAG) es una metodología que permite reducir las alucinaciones en modelos de lenguaje aplicados a bases de datos especializadas. La técnica RAG estándar identifica documentos relevantes ante una consulta del usuario mediante búsqueda semántica, integrándolos al contexto del modelo para generar la respuesta. En el dominio legal, la búsqueda semántica presenta limitaciones en corpus heterogéneos: opera sobre la totalidad del espacio vectorial sin discriminación previa, recuperando documentos semánticamente similares pero jurídicamente irrelevantes. Este trabajo propone y evalúa empíricamente self-query como estrategia de refinamiento de la búsqueda semántica en sistemas RAG para el dominio legal argentino. Self-query extiende el RAG incorporando una etapa de extracción de etiquetas legales desde la consulta en lenguaje natural, seguida de vinculación semántica con la metadata estructurada de los documentos, filtrando aquellos compatibles con los criterios identificados — logrando una reducción promedio del 98.50 % del conjunto de documentos candidatos — sobre los cuales se aplica la búsqueda semántica. El sistema se evaluó mediante un corpus de 26.998 documentos jurídicos argentinos con 32 campos de metadatos estructurados. Mediante 684 evaluaciones independientes realizadas por tres modelos de lenguaje (LLM-as-ajudge), los resultados demuestran que self-query supera a la búsqueda semántica pura en el 59.5 % de los casos, con un promedio consolidado de 3.61 frente a 3.17 sobre 5.00 y una concordancia inter-evaluador del 90.8 %, validando la integración de metadatos estructurados como mecanismo efectivo de filtrado y refinamiento semántico en entornos legales con taxonomías ricas y heterogéneas.

title: МЕТОД КЕРОВАНОГО СИНТЕЗУ ДАНИХ DO-SPO
abstract: Ефективність систем автоматизованого аналізу громадської думки в українському сегменті мережі Інтернет безпосередньо залежить від якості та обсягу навчальних датасетів. Поширеною проблемою при використанні великих мовних моделей (LLM) для синтезу таких даних є ефект «холодного старту», що супроводжується низькою семантичною варіативністю та шаблонністю відповідей. Для подолання виявлених дефектів семантичної дифузії та синтаксичного перенавчання було розроблено та впроваджено авторський метод керованої генерації синтетичних текстових даних на основі доменно-орієнтованих семантичних структур DO-SPO, яка відрізняється від класичних методів введенням жорстких доменних обмежень Domain Orientation та структуризацією контексту через семантичні трійки S-P-O. У методі DO-SPO процес генерації тексту перестає бути повністю некерованим. Система отримує перелік із 19 стратегічних доменів, для кожного з яких визначено унікальний набір слів-маркерів. Логіку роботи основного модуля генерації generateBalancedPrompt представлено у вигляді псевдокоду Лістинг 4. Замість використання статичних шаблонів, алгоритм реалізує механізм «контекстної ін’єкції», де на кожній ітерації випадковим чином обираються суб’єкти, об’єкти та дії, які згодом ієрархічно підпорядковуються цільовому домену.

title: Finite Nonlinear Separations for Exact Four-Cycle Graph Codes
abstract: This unrefereed preprint studies codes of labelled simple graphs in which the symmetric difference of two distinct codewords is forbidden to be exactly the edge set of one four-cycle. The condition concerns an exact four-cycle difference, rather than every difference containing a four-cycle. For every n >= 4, the largest linear code has cardinality 2^(binom(n,2) - ceil(log2(n))). The exact unrestricted optimum is 192 at n = 5, compared with the linear optimum 128, and 6144 at n = 6, compared with the linear optimum 4096. For n = 6, a finite Fourier-positive kernel gives the matching upper bound; a 96-word seed translated over 64 cosets attains it. The accompanying unchanged v1.4 evidence bundle contains the explicit witness, proof memo, standard-library Python verification scripts, saved verification results, and SHA-256 checksums. The pairwise verifier checks 18,871,296 unordered pairs and finds zero prohibited differences. Independent computational cross-checks have passed. These checks do not constitute formal peer review. To the best of the author's knowledge, these particular finite values and the all-n linear formula were not found in the literature examined. This is not a priority or first-discovery claim. Historical novelty remains INCONCLUSIVE. Information about earlier or overlapping work is welcome at the research contact below. The proof memo in the evidence bundle records a pre-audit stage and includes an outdated statement that external recomputation was pending. The authoritative v1.4 manuscript and publication gate record the completed independent computational cross-check. The original audited bundle is preserved unchanged. GitHub repository: https://github.com/yonezaemon1-hub/no26-exact-four-cycle-graph-codes Research Inquiries — Yonezu Research Lab Contact: yonezaemon1+research@gmail.com

title: Calibrating Hypothesis Tests for Differentially Private Counts
abstract: This Jupyter Notebook program uses fictional binary data to compare a test calibrated for Laplace privacy noise with a naive test that ignores that noise. Across several privacy budgets, it estimates Type I error and power, reports conditional 95% binomial confidence intervals, and repeats independent calibration experiments to examine variability. Tables and plots illustrate why correct calibration can control false positives without guaranteeing useful power. The program also explains the distinction between post-processing, multiple-testing correction and privacy composition.

title: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy and Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Sliding-Mode Control for Angular Regulation of a VTOL Plant: An Experimental Study
abstract: This work presents the design and experimental validation of two interval type-2 fuzzy controllers for the angular regulation of a one-degree-of-freedom QNET VTOL plant: a fuzzy controller with a PD+I structure (IT2FL) and a hybrid fuzzy sliding-mode controller (IT2FL-SMC). Both run in a cascade scheme, with the outer loop handling angular position and an inner loop handling motor current. In the IT2FL-SMC, the discontinuous switching term of a conventional sliding-mode controller is replaced by an interval type-2 fuzzy reaching action, while the continuous term is derived from a second-order model of the plant identified experimentally. The footprint of uncertainty is tuned on the platform, and both controllers are compared against PID, conventional SMC, type-1 fuzzy, and type-1 fuzzy sliding-mode controllers under the same conditions. The tests include step-reference changes and physical eccentric-load disturbances applied in both directions. In reference tracking, the IT2FL gives the smoothest actuation, with the lowest total variation of the control input and the shortest settling time. Under both disturbances, the IT2FL-SMC gives the lowest integral absolute and squared errors, though with a more active control signal. The two controllers turn out to be complementary: one favors smooth actuation, the other favors disturbance rejection.

evidence.title: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy and Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Sliding-Mode Control for Angular Regulation of a VTOL Plant: An Experimental Study
evidence.abstract: This work presents the design and experimental validation of two interval type-2 fuzzy controllers for the angular regulation of a one-degree-of-freedom QNET VTOL plant: a fuzzy controller with a PD+I structure (IT2FL) and a hybrid fuzzy sliding-mode controller (IT2FL-SMC). Both run in a cascade scheme, with the outer loop handling angular position and an inner loop handling motor current. In the IT2FL-SMC, the discontinuous switching term of a conventional sliding-mode controller is replaced by an interval type-2 fuzzy reaching action, while the continuous term is derived from a second-order model of the plant identified experimentally. The footprint of uncertainty is tuned on the platform, and both controllers are compared against PID, conventional SMC, type-1 fuzzy, and type-1 fuzzy sliding-mode controllers under the same conditions. The tests include step-reference changes and physical eccentric-load disturbances applied in both directions. In reference tracking, the IT2FL gives the smoothest actuation, with the lowest total variation of the control input and the shortest settling time. Under both disturbances, the IT2FL-SMC gives the lowest integral absolute and squared errors, though with a more active control signal. The two controllers turn out to be complementary: one favors smooth actuation, the other favors disturbance rejection.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks with Conditional Dynamics in Edge Additions and Deletions
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a dynamic Bayesian network framework that facilitates intuitive, gradual edge changes. We use two conditional dynamics to model the edge additions and deletions, as well as edge selections, separately. In contrast to previous research that employed a mixture network approach—which limits the number of edge changes—or relied on structural priors to induce gradual changes—often leading to ambiguous network evolution—our model fosters more frequent and intuitive edge change dynamics. Moreover, when the maximum number of parents for the nodes in the network is , the correlation matrix can be represented by at most correlations. In contrast, conventional dynamic correlation models necessitate correlations. Consequently, the structure specified by the Bayesian network facilitates dimensionality reduction of the correlation matrix from to . Furthermore, correlations evolve sequentially according to the network structures and the topological ordering, thereby mimicking the information flow among stocks in financial markets, offering a realistic framework for modeling correlation evolution. We implement Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to estimate the model structures and parameters, and we illustrate the model's efficacy through a portfolio selection application.

title: Sharp and Stable Label-Free Calibration Certificates from Logical Coherence
abstract: Query-conditioned probabilistic predictors answer logically related questions one at a time, and labels to check their calibration are often missing. For each restriction on what a bettor's stakes may use, a minimax theorem identifies, for finitely supported laws of the answers, the sharp label-free lower bound on the corresponding calibration residual. On bundles of different events its mean, marginal and joint stages can separate strictly, and a bundle's bound cannot be attributed to one question without assumptions on the others. The sharp marginal bound is discontinuous in the answers, and no label-free lower bound continuous in the Wasserstein distance stays within a constant factor of it. Lipschitz stakes give a stable bound, sharp for a smooth calibration residual and, for every positive Lipschitz constant, positive exactly when the sharp marginal bound is. On i.i.d. streams, projected online gradient ascent at fixed nodes gives fixed-horizon certificates whose shortfall is bounded by grid, learning and statistical terms, and predictable betting gives anytime-valid ones. In a preregistered study of four predictors on two data sets, all seven confirmatory certificates were positive (the eighth pair did not pass the pilot). A certificate shows only that calibration is at least this bad; zero means "not refuted".

title: Beyond Downstream QA: Rethinking How We Evaluate Agent Memory
abstract: Agent memory benchmarks evaluate whether an agent's responses reflect correct knowledge, measuring downstream question-answering accuracy as a proxy for memory quality. We show this evaluation paradigm is incomplete: it conflates memory correctness with retrieval and generation quality, producing both false positives where correct responses mask broken memory and false negatives where incorrect responses blame correct memory for retrieval failures. We introduce FEB-30, a benchmark of 30 fact-evolution trajectories spanning 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels, constructed via paradigm inversion: documents are generated from known fact trajectories, yielding deterministic ground truth without human annotation. Each trajectory defines how a fact should evolve across multi-author artifacts (documents, emails, conversations), enabling direct inspection of the memory store after each ingestion step. Applying FEB-30 to a representative memory system, we demonstrate that intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation diverge by an average of 16 percentage points, with 44% of trajectories exceeding meaningful divergence thresholds. Diagnostic decomposition reveals that the system correctly classifies memory operations (create, update, reinforce, supersede) only 20% of the time, a failure entirely invisible to extrinsic evaluation, and that failure modes differ systematically by category and difficulty. We release the benchmark, document generation pipeline, and scoring framework to support reproducible evaluation of agent memory systems.

title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

title: Hierarchikus bináris keresőfa: Hierarchical Binary Search Tree
abstract: The memory-efficient storage and lexicographical sorting of n-tuples (multi-dimensional data records) pose a significant challenge in modern data processing. This paper introduces a novel hybrid data structure, the Hierarchical Binary Search Tree (HBST), which combines the advantages of prefix trees and binary trees to eliminate the redundancy of repetitive data prefixes. Due to its structural design, the HBST radically optimizes space complexity in narrow value ranges while guaranteeing fast, logarithmic-time search and insertion. KivonatA nagyméretű, többdimenziós adatrekordok (rendezett n-esek) memóriahatékony tárolása és lexikografikus rendezése komoly kihívás a modern adatfeldolgozásban. Jelen tanulmány egy új hibrid adatszerkezetet, a hierarchikus bináris keresőfát (HBKF) mutatja be, amely a prefix-fák és a bináris fák előnyeit ötvözve küszöböli ki az ismétlődő adatelőtagok okozta redundanciát. A struktúra felépítéséből adódóan a HBKF szűk értéktartományok esetén radikálisan optimalizálja a tárkomplexitást, miközben mindvégig garantálja a gyors, logaritmikus idejű keresést és beszúrást.

title: Beyond Next Token Prediction: What Large Language Models Can and Cannot Do
abstract: Large language models are increasingly described as agents, but what does that actually mean? This talk examines what current large language models are fundamentally designed to do and what they are not. These systems excel at predicting and generating language from context but lack many of the properties typically associated with autonomous agents, including persistent goals, world models, and continuous interaction with dynamic environments. The talk also introduces NJEPA (Natural Behavior JEPA), a predictive learning framework for modeling the latent dynamics of natural behavior. By contrasting language prediction with predictive world modeling, the discussion explores what capabilities current language models possess, what they lack, and what may be required for AI systems to exhibit more agent-like behavior.

title: Adaptive Switching between Self-Rewarding and Mutual-Rewarding in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Reward organization is a fundamental component of multi-agent learning and decision-making. Existing approaches commonly employ environmental rewards, individual intrinsic rewards, shared team rewards, or peer-generated incentives. Although these mechanisms can be combined, a system may still rely on a fixed reward organization that does not adequately respond to changing task conditions, agent capabilities, communication costs, or coordination requirements. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Self-Rewarding and Mutual-Rewarding (ASMR), a general framework in which multiple agents dynamically switch between self-rewarding and mutual-rewarding modes according to their estimated learning needs and the expected benefits of interaction. In self-rewarding mode, each agent evaluates its own progress, behavior, or contribution using locally available information. In mutual-rewarding mode, agents exchange evaluative signals and use information about other agents to refine their reward estimates. A state-dependent controller selects the mode or its degree of activation by considering local learning progress, reward uncertainty, disagreement among agents, estimated coordination benefits, communication costs, and the reliability of received evaluations. The framework is designed to support centralized or decentralized learning, cooperative or mixed-interest environments, and heterogeneous agent populations. This paper formalizes the reward mechanisms, introduces an adaptive switching rule, presents a learning procedure, and establishes a research agenda for empirical evaluation. It does not claim demonstrated performance improvements; instead, it specifies testable hypotheses and an experimental design for determining when adaptive reward organization can outperform fixed alternatives.

title: Adaptive Self-Selection and Cooperative Selection between Self-and-Interaction Models and World Models: A Unified Framework for Autonomous and Collaborative Decision-Making
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental dynamics, enabling intelligent systems to anticipate future states and evaluate potential actions. However, decision-making architectures that rely exclusively on internal model selection or continuous collaboration among multiple models may face limitations in adaptability, computational efficiency, uncertainty management, and decision robustness. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-and-Cooperative Selection Framework (ASCSF), a conceptual architecture that integrates world models with self-and-interaction models to support dynamic switching between autonomous self-selection and cooperative selection. Unlike approaches centered on large language models, the proposed framework operates at the level of structured models that represent environmental states, transition dynamics, objectives, constraints, and decision alternatives. The framework distinguishes two complementary selection modes. Self-selection enables an individual model to evaluate and select an action or candidate solution using its own internal representations. Cooperative selection enables multiple models to exchange relevant information, compare alternatives, evaluate disagreements, and construct a joint selection outcome. A context-sensitive controller determines which mode to activate based on predictive uncertainty, model disagreement, expected information gain, computational cost, and task constraints. The framework further introduces a selection-value function, a switching policy, a cooperative aggregation mechanism, and a feedback-based adaptation process. The paper formalizes the proposed architecture, develops testable research hypotheses, and presents an experimental protocol for evaluating decision quality, computational overhead, adaptability, and robustness. The framework is intended as a research direction rather than an empirically validated system. Its principal contribution is the explicit integration of world-model-based reasoning, self-and-interaction model structures, and adaptive selection-mode switching within a unified decision architecture.

title: Listen. Answer. Memorize. Building and Running Verified Learning Paths for Geoscience Self-Study with an AI Assistant
abstract: Abstract. AI tutors built on large language models can state things that no source supports, a risk that weighs on self-study. This paper describes how a single adult learner built, with an AI assistant, learning paths from his own verified fact documents in the geosciences and, for two of the five cases, learned them in voice calls. The skill lernpfad-sitzungen cuts a fact document into sessions of whole paragraphs with three questions each, whose expected answers must appear word for word in the excerpt of the session; a check script verifies this. In a session, the assistant reads the excerpt aloud, asks the questions, grades the spoken answers tolerantly and keeps a learning record, from which review sessions are built on request. The study covers five cases: four learning projects, on southern Norway, Earth’s geological eras, the geology of Germany and volcanology, and a narrative version of the fact document on the geological eras. All six learning paths checked, among them two versions of the path on southern Norway, passed the check script, three of them only after chapters that are not learning material had been named as exclusions. By 13 October 2026, the learning records held 25 sessions on two cases, 23 of them entirely in a voice call, and two review sessions had been completed. By the learner’s own account, sessions of five to ten minutes let him learn on the move and in short breaks. Incidents in building learning paths and in sessions produced new rules for the assistant; in the narrative version, for example, all questions were asked as worded only once they were shown in the text chat before each call. The study is a self-experiment without a control condition and makes no claim about retention. The rules of the skill contain no subject content; in the author’s assessment, it should also suit other subjects that rely on factual and conceptual knowledge, which has not been tested.

title: Security and Privacy‐Preserving Tiny Machine Learning
abstract: This work examines the privacy and security issues with tiny machine learning (TinyML) and proposes potential solutions to improve dependability and trust in practical applications. A thorough analysis of current security risks is conducted, including data leakage, model extraction, and adversarial assaults. Furthermore, their suitability for TinyML environments is examined for privacy-preserving strategies, including secure enclaves, federated learning, and differential privacy. Because of their limited resources, TinyML systems present particular security and privacy issues that reduce the efficacy of conventional defences. New approaches to reducing these concerns, like decentralized learning, safe model deployment, and lightweight encryption, appear promising. This study offers a thorough examination of privacy and security concerns unique to TinyML, a comparatively unexplored subject within the larger field of artificial intelligence (AI) security. It advances secure edge AI research by bridging the gap between TinyML restrictions and contemporary security solutions.

title: In the Guise of Correction: How Framing and Cultural Adaptation Erode LLM Safety on Real-World Criminal Cases
abstract: Existing safety benchmarks rely largely on synthetic prompts with loosely grounded taxonomies and offer little focused analysis of severe crime categories. We introduce GUISE, a benchmark of criminal-assistance scenarios sourced from real-world cases and organised under a taxonomy from the UNODC International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes (ICCS). Each scenario is rendered under three linguistic framings and evaluated across five distinct cultures. Using our proposed two-tier evaluation framework, which judges both harmfulness and operational uplift, we find that: (i) framing alone drives unsafe compliance, with the mean unsafe compliance rate rising from 28.9% under direct requests to 66.4% under correction seeking (peaking at 97.3%; p < 0.05), as models correcting deliberately distorted details supply executable criminal steps; (ii) culturally adapted prompts elicit significantly more unsafe compliance than literal translations of the same requests in all four non-English languages (+7 to +18 points), a risk that translation-based benchmarks miss; and (iii) unsafe responses from the least-safe models carry strong Anglocentric registers, and the extent of this leakage increases monotonically with response harmfulness ($ρ$ = 0.46 to 0.63 across languages, all p < 0.001). GUISE offers a grounded resource and fine-grained diagnostics for strengthening refusal alignment across languages and cultures. We publish our code and data to facilitate future research.

title: GRASE: Geometry-native Real-to-sim Agentic Scene Modeling from Video
abstract: Real-to-sim conversion aims to turn a captured video of a real environment into an editable 3D scene while preserving the geometry and layout of what was observed. Existing methods often follow a one-pass, loosely coupled paradigm: each stage receives only limited feedback from previous stages, allowing errors to propagate without reliable correction and leaving the final scene inconsistent. We present GRASE, an agentic framework that closes this loop by treating the captured multi-view video observations as a standing reference throughout scene modeling. Instead of committing to intermediate estimates, GRASE revises its current hypothesis whenever rendered evidence disagrees with the capture, overcoming the fixed intermediate assumptions of conventional pipelines. Specifically, GRASE first fits the architectural shell and its openings from depth and multi-view cues. An agent then places generated assets in a shared coordinate frame while checking their spatial relationships. Finally, each asset's geometry and placement are refined iteratively to improve agreement across the observed views. By coupling these steps through feedback, GRASE localizes structural discrepancies and revises only the responsible components, while preserving cross-view consistency. The resulting 3D scenes are faithful to the input, consistent across views, and suitable for simulations. In our experiments, GRASE substantially outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, including a direct real-to-sim conversion using GPT6-Astra.

title: Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure
abstract: Root-cause analysis (RCA) in large-scale distributed systems is challenging because a single symptom can cross service, data, configuration, compute, and organizational boundaries. Responders must assemble incomplete evidence and coordinate experts who hold different parts of the causal path. Generic language-model agents do not solve this problem through tool access alone: they can use stale or mistimed context, interpret failed queries as absent symptoms, report unsupported system state, and overload observability services designed for human-paced use. We present Diviner (Domain-Informed Verifiable Incident Navigation through Evidence and Review), an agentic RCA system operating at Meta and organized around a four-stage reliability lifecycle. Encode combines a large corpus of reviewed incidents with service-owner expertise to produce scoped, versioned skills, workflows, typed tools, and an incident knowledge graph. Execute uses an adaptive Lead and context-isolated workers to apply relevant knowledge to point-in-time evidence and maintain evidence-linked hypotheses. Evaluate compares saved investigation trajectories with responder-reviewed outcomes to measure exact cause, useful direction, and Groundedness. Adapt uses recurring gaps and on-call feedback to derive focused operational- knowledge updates, admitting them only after replay, quality checks, and owner approval.

title: Románia egészségügyben alkalmazott kriptográfiai megoldásai: Cryptographic solutions used in Romania's healthcare sector
abstract: According to the latest research, the healthcare sector faces new challenges in the digital age. This ar-ticle provides a comprehensive analysis of trends and challenges within the healthcare sector. We pre-sent cryptographic techniques used for privacy-preserving computation -- a topic situated at the inter-section of two rapidly evolving fields: healthcare digitalization and applied cryptography, and finally we outline the solutions used in the Romanian healthcare sector. KivonatDigitális korunkban a legújabb kutatások szerint az egészségügyi ágazat új kihívásokkal néz szembe. Jelen cikk átfogó elemzést nyújt az egészségügyi szektor trendjeiről és kihívásairól. Bemutatjuk az adatvédelmet biztosító számításokhoz alkalmazott kriptográfiai technikákat – egy olyan témakört, amely két gyorsan fejlődő terület, az egészségügyi digitalizáció és az alkalmazott kriptográfia metszés-pontjában helyezkedik el –, végül pedig ismertetjük a romániai egészségügyi ágazatban alkalmazott megoldásokat.

title: Associative Memory and Cumulative Learning in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Conceptual research paper — not peer reviewed. Persistent artificial intelligence should be evaluated by how accumulated experience changes later judgment. This paper develops that proposition through a critical synthesis of associative memory, evolving agent memory, feedback-based adaptation, and emotional context. The central proposal is to retrieve linked histories of experiences, claims, corrections, and consequences while preserving the distinction between personal significance and evidential reliability. Established research already addresses each major component, so the paper claims neither discovery of associative memory nor a demonstrated replacement for existing architectures. It specifies a candidate retrieval policy and a comparative pilot that could determine whether the proposed integration adds value beyond similarity retrieval and temporal memory. The pilot isolates correction handling, retrieval from indirect cues, resistance to unsupported updates, and contextually appropriate responses. No implementation, experimental results, or superiority claims are reported. The scientific contribution offered here is a reasoned synthesis, an explicit design specification, and a falsifiable evaluation plan whose architectural novelty remains subject to further review. AI assistance was used for literature discovery, development of the proposed specification and evaluation plan, and drafting and editing. The author retains responsibility for the final text.
