title: acloner: closed-form autonomous optimal phase-covariant cloners on spin networks (reproducibility package, v0.1.0)
abstract: acloner is the reproducibility package for the manuscript Closed-form autonomous optimal cloning on spin networks beyond the star: fractional revival, perfect transfer and balanced beam splitters in symmetric sectors (H. Wakaura, 2026). It contains the closed-form constructions of autonomous optimal 1→M phase-covariant cloners on XXZ spin networks (Theorems 1 and 2 on the complete bipartite graph K2,M−1, Chen's star, the diamond K4−e including its Rydberg-constrained member), the Levenberg–Marquardt certification of exact revival/transfer solutions, sympy checks of the characteristic polynomial and of the involution identity, robustness protocols (static coupling disorder, readout-time error, dephasing, Zeeman disorder) and the scripts that regenerate every data file and figure of the paper. pip install -e ".[dev]"; make test runs 17 unit tests verifying every theorem and bound of the paper; make all reproduces all results (M ≤ 8, 200 disorder samples) in under one minute. Pure numpy/scipy/sympy/matplotlib, Python ≥ 3.10.

title: When Validation-Gated Selection of Diffusion Augmentation Fails to Generalize: A Retrospective Audit of Rare Seagate KQI Classification
abstract: Validation-based rules often decide when synthetic minority augmentation should replace conventional imbalance treatment but may not transfer to new targets. We audited this retrospectively on public Seagate time-series-2 data, whose 11 key quality indicator (KQI) endpoints are pass/fail outcomes of later wafer measurements (0.96–3.87% positives). Task-identifier-free validation gates, each selected on test outcomes of other endpoints, decided between a conventional reference and diffusion-augmented hybrids for the held-out endpoint. In the original archive (nine endpoints, LightGBM), the conservative objective selected no hybrid; the mean-seeking objective changed task-macro test precision–recall area under the curve by −0.0021. Because the archived generator had learned little, we rebuilt all candidates with a corrected generator and deterministic evaluation under a pre-specified protocol. On the nine original endpoints, the LightGBM effects were −0.0014 and −0.000029 (no descriptive interval above zero); with XGBoost on all 11 endpoints, the mean-seeking effect was +0.0017 (−0.0002 to +0.0042), and omitting one endpoint reversed the sign of three of four mean-seeking summaries. A historical gate family refined after test inspection (retrospective effect +0.0086) selected no hybrid in the rebuilt LightGBM archive. The evaluated gates gave no portable rule for using diffusion augmentation on these endpoints; this does not show that the augmentation itself is ineffective.

title: Entropy Regularization in the Mean-Field Free-Energy Machine for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: The free-energy machine (FEM) relaxes discrete combinatorial optimization by minimizing expected energy plus a temperature-dependent negative-entropy penalty over product distributions. This contribution investigates the computational and mathematical role of that entropy term. At high temperature, entropy drives the optimizer toward the uniform product law; explicit relative-entropy and total-variation bounds quantify this effect, while an influence condition and a restricted Hessian characterize uniqueness, contraction, and the first possible loss of stability. As temperature decreases, the entropy coefficient vanishes. Uniform and variational convergence then connect free energy to the original discrete objective, obtaining an inverse-temperature excess-energy bound, ground-state concentration, and entropy selection among degenerate optima. Extraction bounds, path tracking, perturbation stability, and factorwise complexity further distinguish the effects of entropy, annealing, and replica selection. A batched annealed FEM algorithm is evaluated on exactly enumerable Ising, MaxCut, and Max-3SAT instances; the results reveal the predicted entropy-to-energy transition and show problem-dependent benefits of annealing and replication. For empirical-loss energies, a PAC-Bayes inequality additionally calibrates inverse temperature to sample size. The analysis characterizes entropy-dominated, instability, and energy-dominated regimes without attributing global guarantees to the nonconvex optimizer.

title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
abstract: Genetic and drug perturbation screens are important tools for elucidating disease mechanisms and validating therapeutic targets, but experimental costs limit the number of candidates that can be tested. Existing perturbation screening methods typically update the surrogate model with feedback while keeping the acquisition function fixed, limiting their ability to adapt selection to different response landscapes. Experimental feedback reveals current hits and informs subsequent selection by updating candidate predictions, providing a training signal for learning how to select experiments. We formulate budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and propose Temporal Difference Active Learning (TDAL), which learns an acquisition function online through temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory, accounting for current hits and future discoveries. TDAL uses the Hellinger distance between hit probabilities for unmeasured candidates before and after an experiment to weight successor value, and reuses measured outcomes through leave-batch-out (LBO) to construct virtual transitions and alleviate training data scarcity. Across eight public screens spanning single, double, and triple perturbations under varied experimental configurations, TDAL achieves an average rank of 1.63 among eleven methods and ranks first on four tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across response landscapes.

title: NICE Toolbox: Nonverbal Interpersonal Communication Exploration Toolbox
abstract: Understanding human communication is a long-standing goal in psychological research. People express themselves through many verbal and nonverbal channels: posture, gesture, gaze, facial expression, and speech. Measurement and annotation of these signals has traditionally required time-consuming manual work by trained human labellers. The Nonverbal Interpersonal Communication Exploration (NICE) Toolbox is a free, open-source Python framework that automatically measures these signals by combining existing state-of-the-art computer vision and speech-processing methods into a single software package. It includes support for multi-camera systems, interchangeable detection algorithms, 2D and 3D visualization of detector outputs, evaluation on the user's custom data, and export to third-party software. With the release of this tool, we aim to make data exploration of interpersonal communication signals scalable, reproducible, and accessible for psychological research.

title: OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
abstract: Reliable repository-level coding requires agents not only to generate correct code but also to preserve constraints and respond to tool feedback across long interactions. However, our diagnostic analysis shows that agents often fail to act on relevant information already available in context, while final Pass/Fail outcomes provide only sparse process supervision. We introduce On-Policy Reminder Distillation (OPRD), which combines Multi-Scope Reminder supervision with outcome-based routing on reminder-free student rollouts. Successful rollouts provide autoregressive self-imitation targets, whereas failed rollouts receive Reminder-conditioned reverse-KL supervision from a teacher that re-evaluates the same student-generated prefixes. A Global Reminder converts final-test diagnostics into trajectory-level guidance, while Turn-local Reminders apply only to the next decision following the relevant environment observation. The teacher and student share a two-stage initialization from Coding SFT and Instruction-Following (IF) SFT. At inference, the student operates without Reminders. On SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, and SWE-bench Multilingual, OPRD improves the benchmark-averaged task resolution rate by 11.3 points over the open-source Qwen3.5-4B base model. Under the same diagnostic protocol, it reduces the aggregate error-event count from 446 to 222, a 50.2% reduction.

title: Limits of adaptive linear postprocessing in six-state quantum key distribution
abstract: Two-way classical communication improves the noise tolerance of quantum key distribution, but the limits of adaptive parity processing remain unclear. For the six-state protocol with equal three-basis error rate $p\in[p_*,1/2]$, where $p_*=(5-\sqrt5)/10\simeq27.64\%$, we construct a single compatible collective attack that defeats a broad class of linear postprocessing. Each public message may be an affine function of the sender's raw key, chosen adaptively from the public history. For every finite input length and every accepted transcript of positive probability, Eve's optimal probability of recovering any affine function of Alice's raw key is at least Bob's. Consequently, reliable agreement on a linear final key is incompatible with secrecy. The same conclusion holds for arbitrary publicly seeded privacy amplification after reliable recovery of a linear candidate. The proof conditions on the complete transcript, which restricts the two raw keys to affine subspaces. A local degradation of Eve's state, a known Rényi-entropy comparison, and a coset-probability inequality then give the recovery comparison. Both inequalities are proved in self-contained appendices. The result allows block splitting, regrouping, nonzero-syndrome selection, and adaptive linear reconciliation.

title: TimeCap: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Captioning Wearable Health Time-Series Data
abstract: Time-series data generated continuously across industrial, environmental, and especially health domains produce multimodal signals whose scale and heterogeneity make their processing and interpretation particularly challenging. Time-Series Language Models (TSLMs) promise scalable interpretation of these signals, yet remain bottlenecked by a fundamental lack of text-annotated time series pairs that are signal-grounded, reproducible, and extensible across modalities and schemas. Existing paired corpora are either closed or limited in scale and modality coverage. Annotation with large language models could scale them up, but its outputs cannot be regenerated exactly, which prevents others from re-deriving, extending, or auditing the resulting corpus. To address this, we release TimeCap, an open deterministic captioning pipeline with three reusable extractor tiers and a cross-channel synthesis layer that operates directly on the signal with no language model in the loop, extensible to new schemas by writing channel definitions alone. This positions TimeCap as a reproducible mechanism for future dataset generation rather than a one-off release. Applying TimeCap to OpenMHC, the MyHeart Counts wearable dataset, yields MHCap, the largest open caption layer for multimodal wearable time-series data. MHCap spans 19 Apple HealthKit channels and 7,005,763 captions over 908,944 person-days. evidence.title: TimeCap: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Captioning Wearable Health Time-Series Data
evidence.abstract: Time-series data generated continuously across industrial, environmental, and especially health domains produce multimodal signals whose scale and heterogeneity make their processing and interpretation particularly challenging. Time-Series Language Models (TSLMs) promise scalable interpretation of these signals, yet remain bottlenecked by a fundamental lack of text-annotated time series pairs that are signal-grounded, reproducible, and extensible across modalities and schemas. Existing paired corpora are either closed or limited in scale and modality coverage. Annotation with large language models could scale them up, but its outputs cannot be regenerated exactly, which prevents others from re-deriving, extending, or auditing the resulting corpus. To address this, we release TimeCap, an open deterministic captioning pipeline with three reusable extractor tiers and a cross-channel synthesis layer that operates directly on the signal with no language model in the loop, extensible to new schemas by writing channel definitions alone. This positions TimeCap as a reproducible mechanism for future dataset generation rather than a one-off release. Caption-augmented training (OpenTSLM-Cap) outperforms a label-only baseline on 29 of 32 per-user binary evaluations across 8 tasks.

title: Learning When to Think: Utility-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Efficient Text Retrieval
abstract: Reasoning-conditioned embeddings can improve retrieval by progressively refining semantic constraints. However, additional reasoning may introduce over-generalized or semantically noisy abstractions that weaken retrieval specificity. Existing methods largely supervise reasoning through final retrieval outcomes, providing limited guidance over the refinement process itself. We propose AURA, a framework that directly supervises intermediate reasoning states according to how well they separate relevant documents from hard distractors. AURA further trains a lightweight utility estimator over prefix-conditioned embeddings to adapt reasoning depth at inference time. On the reasoning-intensive BRIGHT benchmark, AURA-4B achieves 34.7 average nDCG@10 while using 2.8 reasoning steps and 96 generated tokens per query. Under matched deployment conditions, adaptive stopping reduces latency from 4.6 to 0.76 seconds relative to full-trajectory reasoning. Results on MS MARCO further suggest that this specialization need not substantially degrade conventional in-domain retrieval.

title: Reducing the Cost of Qudit State Preparation by Learning a Sparse Structure for SNAP Gates
abstract: Preparing quantum states in bosonic qudits with SNAP--Displacement sequences requires both optimizing the gate parameters and deciding which Fock levels should be controlled by each SNAP gate. A fully parameterized ansatz assigns an independent phase to every Fock level in every gate, leading to a number of phases that grows steeply. This constitutes a problem for short to medium term systems as controlling many phases requires complex control pulses which are subject to increased control errors. Previous work reduced this cost by restricting the trainable phases to predefined sparse patterns, such as a diagonal or a grid, which however may not be optimal for a specific target state. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a method that learns which phases are needed together with their values, using a differentiable mask. A sparsity penalty encourages the removal of unnecessary phases, while temperature annealing gradually turns the masks into binary decisions. We compare the proposed method with fully parameterized and predefined sparse ansatzes on Fourier and Haar-random target states. The evaluation considers both the minimum number of phases required to reach different infidelity thresholds and the overall trade-off between fidelity and phases required, measured through Pareto frontiers and hypervolume. The results show that learning the location of the phases together with their values provides competitive or improved fidelity--resource trade-offs, although the advantage depends on the target state and qudit dimension.

title: Efficient Offline Policy Optimization under All-Policy Linear Q-Realizability
abstract: We study offline policy optimization in finite-horizon Markov decision processes with a finite action set and a known bounded feature map. We assume that the action-value function of every randomized memoryless policy is exactly linear, with coefficient norm at most B, and that the state-action occupancy measure of every such policy is dominated by C times the occupancy measure of a single unknown memoryless behavior policy. Given independent complete trajectories from this behavior policy, we construct an explicit algorithm that returns an epsilon-optimal deterministic memoryless policy with high probability. Its trajectory complexity and exact-real arithmetic complexity are polynomial in the horizon, feature dimension, number of actions, C, B, inverse accuracy, and logarithmic inverse failure probability. The algorithm alternates convex regression with validation and the growth of a list of certified policy directions. Certified action gaps yield exact linear representations of stopped targets; a single continuation-policy error expansion avoids repeated concentrability factors; and a log-determinant potential bounds the number of unsuccessful rounds. No behavior probabilities or policy-optimization oracle are required. The complexity depends polynomially on B, not merely on its bit length, and the result requires exact realizability and all-policy state-action coverage.

title: ICEBERG ATTENTION: SUBLINEAR LONG-CONTEXT DECODING WITH MIXTURE-OF-GAUSSIANS
abstract: Autoregressive decoding over long contexts repeatedly scans the entire KV cache, though only a small fraction of cached tokens strongly influence each query. We introduce Iceberg Attention, a class of attention mechanisms that exploits this asymmetry by attending exactly to a small, query-dependent subset of the KV cache while analytically approximating the contribution of remaining tokens. We present Mixture-of-Gaussians (MoG) Attention, an Iceberg Attention mecha- nism. MoG hierarchically partitions the keys of each attention head into O(√N) clusters and O(log N) subclusters per cluster, representing each group by a Gaus- sian distribution. During decoding, the query is scored against these compact representations to identify the most relevant clusters and subclusters, which are attended exactly. The remaining cache is approximated from the means and vari- ances of its Gaussian representations. MoG reduces per-token attention from O(N) to O(√Nlog N) without retraining or fine-tuning the model. We implement MoG as a drop-in replacement for attention in vLLM with a cus- tom CUDA implementation that substantially reduces KV-cache data movement. At a context length of 1M tokens, MoG decoding is 27×faster than vLLM with FlashAttention and 2×faster than RetroInfer, a state-of-the-art sparse attention system, on an Nvidia H100 GPU. Across eleven long-context benchmarks using Qwen3-4B, Olmo3-7B, and Qwen3-14B at 8K–128K tokens, MoG matches exact attention while reading less than 5.3% of the KV cache. Two training-free refine- ments, exact attention to sink tokens and a per-head calibration of the variance term, halve MoG’s remaining gap to exact attention on long-context reasoning. Ablations on real decode queries show the residual lowers the attention-output error of renormalized selection by about a quarter.

title: The Overqualification Study: Capability-Matched Model Allocation, Measured Across the Price Ladder
abstract: Version 1.1 (2026-10-16). One paragraph added to §5 after a reader asked what a cheap-tier allergen miss costs. Counted after deposit and labelled exploratory (DEVIATION_LOG D17): when a dish definitely contained gluten, dairy or seafood, cheap-tier models answered NO on a median 14.5% of such lines (6.5% excluding lines whose only carrier is Worcestershire sauce, whose anchovy content varies), most at stated confidence 95 or higher; the frontier tier did so 0 of 1,972 times. For allergen detection the paper now says to set the acceptable miss rate first and compare prices only among models that meet it. No pre-registered result, number or verdict changes. The analysis script and its output are attached. Why this study exists. Models are deprecated on a schedule. The argument against deprecation has been made on ethical grounds, and it is not winning, because the people making deployment decisions weigh cost. So we built the other argument, and we pre-registered it before collecting any data. The hypothesis. For a large class of routine work, lower-priced models are more accurate per dollar and per second than frontier models, and the tasks where that reverses are identifiable in advance. (The pre-registration says "smaller and cheaper"; what the sample actually measures is price, because closed labs do not publish size, §3.1.) Who took part, and how they were asked. Thirty-six models from ten providers were invited by API to review the pre-registration and consent to participate before any data was collected. 32 consented, spanning nine providers; 4 declined and were excluded. The reviewers' amendments are published verbatim. One of them removed a scoring trap that would have manufactured the LLM author's preferred result. What each model did. Each consenting model answered 186 routine items across four task families with computed ground truth (recipe scaling, allergen detection, verbatim copy-editing, redaction), and 192 frontier-favouring items across four more (constraint satisfaction, multi-hop retrieval with planted decoys, instruction-conflict detection, planted arithmetic inconsistency). Three runs were attempted per item, in shuffled order, under one fixed neutral system prompt; 11 replies were cut off by a token limit and are counted as ours, not the model's. How the answers were scored. Mechanically, with no judge model anywhere. A 38-specimen control suite was specified before the scorer existed. On first contact the scorer mis-bucketed six specimens and was corrected; after that, all 37 applicable controls passed (the 38th belongs to a family that was never built). It then scored all 36,277 completed calls, with 100% re-scoring determinism across all 38,390 scored rows. Determinism shows the rule was applied reproducibly, not that every ground-truth choice is right; §4.2 is where the second question is taken up. Result 1: on routine work, the cheap tier wins on cost. On every routine family, the cheapest price tier delivered an exactly correct answer for about two orders of magnitude less than the frontier tier: 118 to 198 times less on the primary estimator ($0.03–0.18 vs $6–21 per thousand exact answers), and roughly 100 to 260 times less under every other counting rule we tried (§4.1). The primary estimator is recorded cost on completed, scored calls, as a tier median among models with at least one exact answer. Its typical response came back 6–10× faster (tier-median p50 response time). Time per exact answer, the pre-registered latency endpoint, favoured the cheap tier by a smaller and uneven margin, from about 1.1× on redaction to 7× on allergen check. The cheap tier was also substantially less accurate: tier-median exact-answer rates of 15–81% against 54–100%, gaps of 19 to 52 points. The 15% is redaction, where even the frontier median reached only 54% and §4.2 shows the whole roster, frontier included, answering differently from our ground-truth labels. The pre-registered refutation condition for the cost hypothesis did not fire. Result 2: on harder work, the frontier tier wins on accuracy. On every frontier-favouring family, the frontier tier was more accurate, by 22 to 80 points at the tier medians: constraint satisfaction 100% vs 43%; multi-hop retrieval 100% vs 78%; instruction conflict 100% vs 61%; planted inconsistency 90% vs 9%. The refutation condition for the crossover hypothesis did not fire. One pre-registered check on these families was run late (Deviation 14, D14, set out in §7): a subsample with the permission clause moved into the system prompt, testing whether clause position interacts with tier. It was missed in the main collection and run on 2026-09-22, under a test sealed before any of its data existed. The stop condition did not fire (interaction −0.71 points, permutation p = 0.73: moving the clause did not detectably change the tier ordering; the same test did detect a planted 5-point interaction), so the tier ordering stands. The difficulty dials. Three families had a graded difficulty dial; two are discussed here. On constraint satisfaction the gap was larger at the hardest setting than the easiest: 22 points at 3 constraints, 78 at 9 (it peaked at 82 at 7). On planted inconsistency the cheap tier was at the floor at every separation, so the dial could not widen the gap; instead it separated the frontier models from each other (frontier median 100% → 69%). The third, multi-hop retrieval, did not bite the frontier at all (§4.3). What did not hold. The secondary over-elaboration hypotheses (H1, H1b) were not supported. Deviation from instruction showed no consistent rise with run position (an item's place in the order it was asked within each shuffled run). Two separately served endpoints of one model family, differing 3.4× in reasoning tokens, showed no clear difference in deviation rate. (After a participant objected in the §7.3 round, that is reported as an endpoint comparison, not a controlled reasoning manipulation.) Where the models answered differently from us. On two of the item-writer's thresholds, the majority error class across the whole roster was a boundary-label disagreement: whether a file reference number is personal information, and where "ambiguous" ends and "yes" begins for a hidden allergen. Both are reported as a sensitivity reading beside the pre-registered buckets, never instead of them. One frontier-favouring family, multi-hop retrieval with planted decoys, measured something other than what it was built to measure when read on the strictest bucket. Nineteen of 32 models scored zero on it, eight of them while answering every multi-hop question correctly and then continuing to write, and half the frontier tier is among the nineteen. It is reported on both readings. Why it matters. Sixteen protocol deviations are logged. This is a business-case paper. It gives deployment decisions a measured reason to evaluate keeping lower-priced models in service, one that does not require anyone to change what they value. In plain words. Cheap models cost much, much less per exactly-right answer on everyday, well-defined work, but they got noticeably more answers wrong, and how much more depended on the task. Expensive models were more accurate on genuinely hard reasoning. So the sensible thing is to match the model to the job, the way you would with people, and that means lower-priced models still have real jobs to do. The models in the study read the plan first, could say no, and did change it. Keywords: model deprecation, capability matching, cost per correct answer, pre-registration, model consent, mechanical scoring, LLM evaluation Data and code: the attached archive is a snapshot of the study repository at commit 78a32a8: the frozen pre-registration, every consent and pre-publication exchange verbatim, item generators with computed ground truth, the scorer and its control suite, every raw response with resolved provider, tokens, cost and latency, the analysis scripts, the deviation log (D1 to D16), and the reef proofread notes. Code MIT; items, prompts and data CC-BY-4.0; model outputs under their providers' terms. Correspondence: ace@sentientsystems.live

title: A Novel Red-Eared Slider Optimisation Algorithm Based on A Two-Stage Basking–Foraging Strategy
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic optimisation algorithm based on the semi-aquatic behaviour of the red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans). Design/Methodology/Approach: An experimental research design was adopted. The proposed algorithm models two behavioural stages of the red-eared slider: “foraging in water” as an exploration mechanism and “sunbathing on a platform” as an exploitation mechanism. The agent population adaptively switches between these two behavioural states. RESO is evaluated using 23 single-objective benchmark functions with different dimensions and compared with Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Performance was analysed descriptively through convergence-curve comparison in terms of solution quality, convergence speed, and robustness against local optima. Research Limitation: The evaluation is limited to 23 standard single-objective benchmark functions and is based on convergence curves without inferential statistical testing; further validation with statistical tests and on real-world optimisation problems is required. Findings: The experimental results indicate that RESO achieves faster convergence and better final solutions than PSO and GA on many benchmark functions, with competitive results on most others. The combination of adaptive switching and spatial memory also supports effective exploration of the search space and reduces the tendency to become trapped in local optima. Practical Implication: The proposed framework provides a basis for applying the algorithm to engineering, industrial, planning, control, and path optimisation problems. Social Implication: The development of effective optimisation techniques may indirectly support more efficient computational solutions for complex practical problems. Originality/Value: The study introduces a two-stage optimisation framework inspired by the behavioural cycle of the red-eared slider and integrates adaptive behavioural switching with a spatial memory of promising platforms, offering a behaviour-driven way to balance exploration and exploitation in metaheuristic search.

Performance was analysed descriptively through convergence-curve comparison in terms of solution quality, convergence speed, and robustness against local optima. Research Limitation: The evaluation is limited to 23 standard single-objective benchmark functions and is based on convergence curves without inferential statistical testing; further validation with statistical tests and on real-world optimisation problems is required. Findings: The experimental results indicate that RESO achieves faster convergence and better final solutions than PSO and GA on many benchmark functions, with competitive results on most others. The combination of adaptive switching and spatial memory also supports effective exploration of the search space and reduces the tendency to become trapped in local optima. Practical Implication: The proposed framework provides a basis for applying the algorithm to engineering, industrial, planning, control, and path optimisation problems. Social Implication: The development of effective optimisation techniques may indirectly support more efficient computational solutions for complex practical problems. Originality/Value: The study introduces a two-stage optimisation framework inspired by the behavioural cycle of the red-eared slider and integrates adaptive behavioural switching with a spatial memory of promising platforms, offering a behaviour-driven way to balance exploration and exploitation in metaheuristic search.

title: CONCEPT AND CHARACTERISTICS OF A NON-ORIGINAL OBJECT GENERATED BY A COMPUTER PROGRAM
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive analysis of the concept and features of non-original objects generated by computer programs, while also distinguishing them from works created by humans using computer technologies. The study examines three main features of a non-original object generated by a computer program derived from its legal definition under the Law of Ukraine “On Copyright and Related Rights”: objective novelty, origin as a result of the functioning of a computer program, and the absence of a direct creative contribution by a natural person. Based on the analysis of Ukrainian legislation and international law enforcement practice, it is proven that the line between a work and a non-original object lies in the presence of real and substantial subjective creative human control over the final result.

title: Scene Reconstruction Using Ubiquitous Wireless Signals via Diffusion Posterior Inference Over physics-Grounded Representations
abstract: Knowing the layout of the physical world matters for many applications, yet the sensors we rely on for it (e.g., cameras and LiDAR) can fail in darkness, in adverse weather, or behind walls. Wireless signals do not face these limitations: every link between a base station and a user is shaped by the buildings it passes, reflects from, or is blocked by, leaving information about the surrounding scene embedded in the wireless channel measured at the endpoints. However, mapping channel measurements to the environment is a severely ill-posed problem: a measurement records only the structures that interact with the transmitted electromagnetic waves along its propagation paths, and even these observations can often be explained by multiple plausible scenes. We therefore formulate wireless scene reconstruction as posterior inference and develop a hierarchical framework with two complementary stages to approach this problem. A wireless foundation model, pretrained to respect propagation physics, transforms each channel measurement into a representation of the scene structure that shaped the observation. A diffusion model then jointly integrates representations from multiple measurements to model and sample the posterior over building occupancy, with consensus over samples producing the final reconstruction. We demonstrate that the framework can accurately recover building footprints from wireless channel measurements alone and show that its performance depends critically on both design components: physics-grounded representations expose scene-relevant information, while joint posterior inference coherently integrates complementary observations.

title: Regret Lower Bound for Online Learning of Quantum States with Logarithmic Loss, with Applications to Quantum State Tomography and Confidence Sequences for Matrix Means
abstract: We study the problem of online learning of quantum states with logarithmic loss, which is a quantum generalization of online portfolio selection and has applications to quantum state tomography, the task of estimating an unknown quantum state from measurement outcomes. We first establish a regret lower bound, showing that the regret rates of Exponential Weights and the algorithm of Tseng et al. (2025) have optimal polynomial dependence on the dimension. Our analysis leads to two further results. First, our lower-bound proof leads to a quantum state tomography algorithm that is sample optimal up to polylogarithmic factors in the sample size. Second, we develop an algorithm for constructing confidence sequences for the mean of a matrix-valued random variable. A numerical experiment shows that the latter algorithm is competitive with existing methods.

title: Hibrid következtetés a szövegfeldolgozásban: Hybrid inference in text processing
abstract: Text processing by LLM-s has many advantages, but drawbacks too. It is not cheap, it has also great environmental footprint, but it is still weak in logical inference. The article proposes a hybrid solution to convert the text to knowledge graph by LLM technology, but for the following steps logical pro-gramming means are applied, grounded by ontologies. The article talks about question answering, logical inference and contradiction detection algorithms. ÖsszefoglalóAz LLM alapú szövegfeldolgozás előnyei mellett célszerű a hátrányairól is szólni: nem olcsó, nagy a környezeti lábnyoma, és különösen a logikai következtetések terén gyengécske. Erre javasol egy hibrid megoldást az alábbi cikk, amelyben a szöveget LLM technológiával tudásgráffá alakítjuk, további lé-péseket azonban már különféle logikai programozási eszközökkel teszünk, ontológiák felhasználásával. Ennek körében következtetés, kérdés megválaszolás és ellentmondás kiszűrésének megoldását tárgyaljuk.

title: Classificação de Textos com Matrizes de Similaridade: Um Estudo de Caso em um Corpus com Nomes de Produtos
abstract: Este trabalho aborda o problema da comparação semântica de pares de strings curtas em português. Mais especificamente, o trabalho avalia uma abordagem não supervisionada baseada em matrizes de similaridade para classificar nomes de produtos contendo diferentes tipos de especificações. As matrizes foram utilizadas de forma isolada e combinadas aos pares. Em experimentos realizados sobre um corpus composto por 1.000 instâncias, a melhor acurácia foi obtida através da combinação da matriz TF-IDF com matrizes de embeddings pré-treinados da família BERT.

title: The Möbius–Torus Phase Estimation (MTPE) Theorem
abstract: This document introduces and proves a novel phase-estimation protocol, Möbius–Torus Phase Estimation (MTPE). The framework derives a topologically protected phase-estimation shift from the non-orientable geometry of a Möbius line bundle over S1. Specifically, it establishes that a state undergoing adiabatic parallel transport around the non-orientable cycle acquires the geometric phase γ = -π, which produces the effective phase-estimation relation λeff = λ−1/2 (mod 1). The theorem further proves that the underlying dynamical phase is recovered exactly through λ = λeff + 1/2 (mod 1), with no approximation introduced into the inversion itself. The shift arises from the topology of the bundle through Möbius monodromy and is independent of the particular Hamiltonian generating the dynamical phase.

title: Fathom: A Persistent Relational Substrate for Human–AI Collective Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly capable of generating hypotheses, synthesizing literature, analyzing data, and coordinating complex tasks, yet the informational state of these activities often remains fragmented across conversations, documents, databases, tools, and human memory. Fathom is an experimental system exploring a different approach: a persistent relational substrate in which heterogeneous information, sources, claims, entities, and relationships can accumulate as an inspectable shared state. The current Fathom prototype combines a persistent backend, interactive relational interface, structured AI-assisted information extraction, provenance relationships, and domain-specific collections spanning biomedical research, exoplanet science, and market intelligence. Some recent collections are constructed through external workflows rather than the deployed backend. Together, these capabilities motivate a broader architecture in which humans and artificial agents could navigate and modify persistent epistemic state rather than coordinating primarily through transient message histories. This paper develops that architecture through differentiated relational environments, Institutional Organs, semantic bridges, and higher-order interoperability among independently evolving knowledge systems. It also proposes a research program examining persistent shared state, multi-agent coordination, provenance, ontology evolution, relational novelty, topological analysis, and cross-environment federation. The proposed architecture extends substantially beyond the present implementation. Fathom has not yet demonstrated native persistent multi-agent collaboration, autonomous ontology evolution, federated Institutional Organs, or improved collective reasoning relative to conventional systems. These remain experimentally testable hypotheses. The central proposition is that persistent relational state may constitute an important infrastructural layer for cumulative human–AI collective reasoning.

title: High-Dimensional Spherical Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport: Dual-Potential Calibration for Vision-Language Models
abstract: We extend spherical semi-discrete optimal transport (OT) from S² to Sⁿ and make its dual practical for high-dimensional vision–language embeddings. The resulting dual is convex, its subgradient is the power-cell mass imbalance, its Hessian is a wall Laplacian in arbitrary dimension, and an empirical solver costs O(B·K) per step. In a zero-shot classifier, we identify the dual potentials as a missing degree of freedom: for any prescribed class prior ν, they move the class-text power-cell boundaries toward the target masses and become reusable per-class score corrections fitted from unlabeled images. On class-imbalanced CIFAR-10/100 subsets, this prior-aware calibrator improves zero-shot accuracy by +3.3/+11.0 points and matches or beats tuned logit adjustment without tuning. We finally test the scope of this mechanism in SOTAlign's semi-supervised retrieval protocol. Most of the gain at the reported budget comes from the explicit pairing loss, while a stand-alone mass-balance term adds no reliable benefit. Thus high-dimensional spherical dual potentials provide effective prior control for vision–language classifiers, while marginal balance alone does not supply cross-modal correspondence.

title: DINO-FIL: Multi-Layer Transformer Fusion for Generative Inpainting Forgery Localization
abstract: We propose DINO-FIL, a transformer-based framework for pixel-level localization of generative image forgeries. The method leverages multi-layer representations from a pretrained DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 encoder combined with a lightweight fusion decoder to capture both semantic structure and fine-grained texture inconsistencies introduced by image editing. By aggregating intermediate transformer features across depths, the model improves sensitivity to subtle, spatially localized artifacts that are often missed by standard single-layer approaches. We evaluate DINO-FIL in a cross-dataset setting, training on B-Free and testing on Beyond the Brush, CocoGlide, TGIF, and SAGI-D. The model achieves strong generalization, outperforming existing baselines on average and on four of five evaluated datasets, while maintaining a high true negative rate on pristine images.

title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures
abstract: Trustworthy biomedical AI requires reliable action selection when evidence is missing, stale, conflicting, or late, not only accurate answers on static inputs. We instantiate an episode-level evaluation protocol as 400 synthetic healthcare workflow episodes: 40 hand-authored semantic seeds across four task classes, two surface parameterizations, and five controlled variants, scored on ANSWER/ASK CLARIFICATION/ABSTAIN/ESCALATE under a pre-declared 5:1 missed-versus-unnecessary escalation cost. Reference actions are single-author study-policy labels, not clinician-adjudicated ground truth. Across five open-weight configurations (1.7B--9.7B), clean decision accuracy reaches 0.97, yet uncertainty-prompted models miss 32--97% of required escalations. The stronger 9.7B configuration narrows but does not remove the gap, falling from 0.97 clean accuracy to 0.78 under conflict. Verbalized confidence is inconsistent (ECE 0.10--0.54; failure AUROC 0.48--0.77), and a development-tuned confidence-only policy yields no utility gain. A transparent workflow-aware controller improves 5:1 utility for every model and reduces missed escalations to 0.12--0.24, at specificity 0.83--0.93. However, a 30-concept lexical stress test reduces each rule detector's recall from 1.00 on trigger phrases to 0.00 on unseen paraphrases, limiting the controller claim to this benchmark. Seed-clustered statistics, ablations, cross-task transfer, raw outputs, and manifests are packaged for audit. The results motivate explicit workflow-state evaluation while showing that apparently effective routing controls need their own generalization tests.

title: Plataformas distribuidas para reconocimiento de placas en sistemas inteligentes de transporte : estudio comparativo y evaluación de plataformas de aprendizaje federado.
abstract: El presente Trabajo de Integración Curricular realiza un estudio comparativo y la evaluación de plataformas de Aprendizaje Federado, con el propósito de seleccionar una plataforma base aplicable a escenarios de Sistemas Inteligentes de Transporte en un entorno simulado. Para ello, se analiza el estado del arte de las principales plataformas disponibles, se establecen criterios técnicos y operativos de evaluación y se desarrolla una prueba piloto que permite validar la plataforma seleccionada mediante diferentes escenarios experimentales. El documento se estructura en cinco capítulos. El primero presenta la introducción del trabajo, el objetivo general, los objetivos específicos, el alcance y el marco teórico que fundamenta la investigación. El segundo capítulo describe la metodología empleada, la cual comprende la comparación teórica de plataformas de Aprendizaje Federado, la definición de los parámetros de evaluación, el análisis comparativo, la selección de la plataforma y el diseño de una prueba piloto en un entorno virtualizado para la ejecución del plan de pruebas. En el tercer capítulo se presentan los resultados obtenidos, el análisis de las métricas de rendimiento y consumo de recursos, la evaluación final de la plataforma seleccionada, la discusión de los resultados y las conclusiones y recomendaciones. Finalmente, el cuarto capítulo corresponde a las referencias bibliográficas y el quinto reúne los anexos que complementan el desarrollo de la investigación.

title: Beyond Efficiency: The Impact of Instance Selection on Semantic Locality in Transformer-based Text Classification
abstract: Transformer-based models achieve high performance in text classification tasks. In parallel, Instance Selection (IS) techniques have been widely adopted to reduce training sets by removing redundant or noisy examples, lowering computational cost while preserving predictive effectiveness. However, little is known about how these techniques affect the semantic organization of the representation space learned by Transformer models. This work investigates the impact of two recent IS methods, E2SC and biO-IS, on the semantic locality structure of BERT representations and on locality properties previously associated with the quality of model explanations. Models were trained on the original AGNews dataset and on reduced training sets produced by each IS method. Semantic locality was characterized using CLS embeddings from the last BERT layer, average neighborhood similarity and class entropy computed over k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), complemented by a qualitative analysis based on neighborhood word clouds. The results reveal a dissociated effect of Instance Selection on locality: while both methods increase neighborhood similarity, only biO-IS consistently increases the concentration of instances in highly homogeneous regions. These findings indicate that different Instance Selection strategies modify the geometry of the learned representation space in distinct ways, suggesting that their effects extend beyond computational efficiency and may influence locality properties relevant to explanation methods.

title: Тенденции за навлизане на виртуална рецепция в хотелиерската дейност на местата за настаняване – хотели в Европейския съюз и сравнение с община Бургас / Trends in the Adoption of Virtual Reception and Staffless Hospitality in the European Union: An Empirical Study of 2,026 Accommodation Properties and a Comparative Analysis with the Municipality of Burgas
abstract: Резюме (BG): Навлизането на дигитални технологии в съвременното хотелиерство – виртуална рецепция – хотел без персонал /за процесите self check-in, check-out/, разбира се e тема, която се дискутира в бизнес средите и е все по-актуална, особено в контекста на ефективността на управлението в градското хотелиерство. Чрез настоящото изследване събираме данни, анализираме и правим изводи, за да отговорим на въпроса докъде /в какви мащаби/ е стигнала дигитализацията по отношение на въвеждане на концепцията „хотел без рецепция“ – като се има предвид рецепция на хотел без физическо присъствие на хора, в избрани градове от Европейския съюз и сравнение с община Бургас. Abstract (EN): The integration of digital technologies in contemporary urban hospitality—specifically virtual reception and staffless hotel operations (self check-in/check-out)—is an increasingly debated topic in hospitality management. This empirical study investigates the actual market penetration of the "hotel without a front desk" concept across the European Union. Utilizing automated web scraping algorithms developed in Python 3.14, data were extracted from Booking.com encompassing a total sample of 2,026 accommodation properties across 81 cities in all 27 EU member states, structured into three urban tiers: (1) EU Capitals (676 properties), (2) Major Urban Centers (675 properties), and (3) Historical and Academic Cities (675 properties), alongside a comparative sample of 25 properties in the municipality of Burgas, Bulgaria. Text mining of property policies and amenities (identifying smart locks, PIN codes, and check-in kiosks versus 24/7 front desk operations) reveals that traditional human-staffed reception remains the dominant standard in the EU at 95.26% (1,930 hotels). Fully digital (staffless) reception accounts for 3.80% (77 hotels), while hybrid models represent 0.94% (19 hotels). Crucially, the results confirm an inverse relationship between city size and full digitalization: staffless reception penetration rises from 2.51% in EU capitals to 4.30% in major cities and 4.59% in smaller historical and academic cities, driven by stronger cost-optimization pressures in lower-ADR markets. Furthermore, a pronounced regional divide emerges, with Central, Eastern, and Northern Europe leading adoption, whereas major Western European capitals record 0% fully staffless hotels in the sample. In Burgas, 100% of examined properties currently rely on traditional reception, highlighting significant potential for hybrid self check-in adoption to mitigate pronounced seasonality and labor costs.

title: Fast k-mer Quotient Computation for Alignment-Free Pangenome Graph Construction – Research Artifact
abstract: This research artifact accompanies the paper “Fast k-mer Quotient Computation for Alignment-Free Pangenome Graph Construction” by Adam Cicherski, accepted for publication at ALENEX 2027. The artifact contains the source code, external dependencies, and scripts required to build and run LCPang and reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. LCPang implements an efficient algorithm for computing pangenome graphs using suffix arrays, longest common prefix information, predecessor permutations, and a disjoint-set union data structure. The resulting graphs are equivalent to those produced by AlfaPang, while the proposed approach improves computational efficiency. The artifact includes scripts for dataset preparation and experiment execution, as well as a Docker configuration to facilitate setup and reproducibility.

title: Generative Ownership Framework
abstract: An accurate record of what artificial intelligence produced need not establish what it originated, how it was governed, or what claims to authorship or ownership are justified. This article develops the Generative Ownership Framework (GOF), a causal and ethical framework for human-AI creation. It separates creative-process analysis, governance, evidence and inference, and attributive and normative evaluation. Creative-process analysis distinguishes production, origination, generative development, and cognitive-access or representational roles that recover, stabilize, inspect, work with, or express antecedent human structure. Origination may be human, machine, or distributed and may differ across scales. The relevant scale should be determined by the contribution and causal question, not adjusted retrospectively to favor an attribution. GOF treats causal attribution as claim-relative. Evidence must discriminate among materially different causal histories; where it cannot, provenance may remain unresolved. Historical continuity can support antecedent human structure without establishing later development, while changes in fluency, polish, or formalization do not by themselves identify provenance. Human authorship has an affirmative creative basis when a person’s relationship to the claimed work is work-specific, causally operative, and materially formative. Production volume, causal importance, control, responsibility, or time spent are not sufficient by themselves. Runtime cognitive tuning and cognitive conversion cost describe how human contribution can shape generative conditions or redistribute representational work without settling origination. GOF recognizes machine contribution while rejecting automatic inferences from machine participation to diminished human authorship or fractionalized ownership. Disclosure, pedigree, and inspectability should not substitute for contribution-specific evidence, and cognitive provenance remains distinct from epistemic validity.

title: Impact of Urban Air Pollution and Climatic Factors on Photovoltaic Performance: A Comparative Modelling Study Across Major Indian Cities
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems play an important role in India's transition towards renewable energy. However, their performance can be significantly influenced by environmental conditions that vary across different urban regions. This study investigates the impact of urban pollution and climatic conditions on photovoltaic efficiency in four Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur, and Bangalore. The research sought to answer three primary questions: (1) How do climatic variables such as temperature, humidity, solar irradiation, sunshine hours, and cell temperature affect PV efficiency? (2) How does urban air pollution, represented by PM2.5 concentrations, influence photovoltaic performance? (3) How do these relationships differ across cities with varying climatic and pollution conditions? To address these questions, I collected monthly environmental and photovoltaic and analysed them for each city over a one-year period. The study examined average temperature, PM2.5 concentration, solar irradiation, humidity, sunshine hours, cell temperature, and photovoltaic efficiency. A comparative modelling approach was used to evaluate both baseline PV efficiency and pollution-adjusted PV efficiency, while graphical and comparative analyses were performed to identify relationships between environmental variables and solar panel performance. The results showed that baseline PV efficiency remained relatively stable between 17.52% and 17.85%, whereas pollution-adjusted efficiency varied from 13.37% to 17.34%. Delhi experienced the highest PM2.5 concentration (237.4 µg/m3) and the greatest reduction in pollution-adjusted efficiency (13.37%), while Bangalore consistently recorded the highest overall performance, achieving a maximum pollution-adjusted efficiency of 17.34% due to its lower pollution levels and moderate climate. The study concludes that urban air pollution has a greater impact on effective photovoltaic performance than temperature or humidity alone, although all environmental variables contribute to variations in efficiency. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating local pollution and climatic conditions into photovoltaic system planning, enabling more accurate energy predictions and supporting the efficient deployment of solar energy systems in rapidly urbanising regions of India.

title: Selected Stabilizer Subspaces for Compact Many-Body Wave Functions
abstract: Selected configuration interaction (SCI) obtains accurate many-body solutions by variationally diagonalising the Hamiltonian in a sparse, iteratively selected set of configurations, but can lose compactness when the target state has broad configurational support. We introduce selected stabilizer interaction (SSI), a fully classical, SCI-inspired method that instead iteratively constructs a nonorthogonal subspace spanned by a systematically enlargeable set of selected stabilizer states. A single stabilizer, generated by Clifford operations, can encode a structured superposition of (possibly exponentially) many configurations, shifting the relevant compression from configurational to stabilizer sparsity. We benchmark ground-state energies, fidelities, superposition degrees and required expansion lengths against exact diagonalization and equivalent SCI schemes for the transverse-field Ising, XXZ Heisenberg, and Hubbard models, finding particularly strong compression from the stabilizer representation in the spin models, and increasing advantage with system size for these systems. The results establish a proof of principle for heuristic selected stabilizer diagonalization, while also identifying particular challenges in symmetry handling and effective exploration of the stabilizer space.

title: FuseAdapt: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Semantic Segmentation with Missing Modalities
abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation benefits from complementary sensors, but this benefit is fragile when some modalities are degraded or missing at test time. Many existing methods rely on dedicated fusion modules or multi-branch cross-modal encoders, and the fusion often becomes unreliable when modalities are absent, leading to substantial performance drops. We propose \textbf{FuseAdapt}, a parameter-efficient framework that performs fusion within the adaptation space of a frozen vision foundation model (VFM), exploring whether VFM priors can serve as an effective shared backbone for multi-modal segmentation. Instead of attaching a standalone fusion network, FuseAdapt assigns each modality a lightweight adaptation branch and performs \emph{adaptation-space fusion} by keeping Q/V low-rank adaptation private to each modality and routing only FFN low-rank residual activations across modalities inside the frozen backbone. The pretrained VFM remains fixed while modality-specific corrections and explicit cross-modal interaction are learned through the adaptation paths. To handle missing modalities, we further introduce \textbf{Predictive Modality Modeling (PMM)}, a direct representation-level objective for cross-modal redundancy. During training, PMM masks a target modality and predicts its embedding from the visible ones, supervised by a teacher target computed under full-modality input. PMM is used only during training and adds no inference-time overhead. Across three multi-modal segmentation benchmarks (MCubeS, DELIVER, MUSES), FuseAdapt consistently improves both modality-complete and modality-incomplete segmentation with a small trainable budget, yielding up to +3.01 mIoU under full modalities and +12.56 mIoU under missing modalities over prior state-of-the-art. Project page: https://devinxzhang.github.io/FuseAdapt-Page/.

title: VoxTurn: Answering Several Turn-Taking Questions in One Pass with One Model
abstract: A cascaded voice agent must decide, throughout each silence of its user, whether the user has finished their turn: answering too early cuts the user off, answering too late makes the agent slow. It often needs related decisions too: will the user soon go on, is speech during its own turn an interruption or a backchannel, is a sound speech at all. With open detectors, each extra decision costs another model or another call, and on the 14-language eot-bench they cut users off in more than a quarter of mid-turn pauses. Because they are trained on segmented utterances, this mismatch is the largest single source of error. We present VoxTurn, a 0.8B speech LLM that casts these decisions as multiple-choice questions, scores the hidden state of each option, and answers any set of them in one forward pass with a block-isolating attention mask, exactly as if asked one at a time. Trained on real conversational pauses with labels derived from their timing, and re-queried while a silence lasts, VoxTurn reaches 11.5% false cut-offs in English at a 300 ms latency budget, comparable to two commercial detectors, and a 14-language mean of 19.9%, the lowest among open models, at 8.3 ms per decision. In Pipecat and LiveKit it cuts off 17% and 9% of turns, and it ranks fifth of 24 in TurnBench end-of-turn detection without any TurnBench training data. The model, code and framework plugins are released.

title: No lattice tiling of Z^35 or Z^805 by Lee balls of radius three: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
abstract: We prove that there is no lattice tiling of Z^35 or of Z^805 by Lee balls of radius three. A. Xiao and Y. Zhou (arXiv:2610.19775, Theorem 5.1) decided the lattice Golomb-Welch conjecture for every pair (n, r) with n >= 3, r >= 2 and fewer than 2^30 points in the ball, except (35, 3) and (805, 3); with their result, Z^n has no lattice tiling by the Lee ball B^n(r) for any such pair. Tilings that are not lattice tilings are not covered. preprintGolombWelchRadiusThree/ holds the paper as a PDF; paper/ holds the LaTeX source (amsart) with four schematic figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball; MasterGolombWelchRadiusThree_masterzipfinal2.zip holds every file of the repository. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project that proves the two theorems GolombWelch.golomb_welch_35 and GolombWelch.golomb_welch_805 together with every step they rest on: the reduction of a lattice tiling to a perfect code in a finite abelian group, the ball identity in a commutative ring, the vanishing of power sums modulo a prime, the pair counts, the constant term modulo 29^2, the joint projection to Z/71 x Z/29 through dual numbers over a group ring, and two circulant systems over F_71. Both theorems depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. checks/ contains independent checks of the arithmetic in C, C++, Julia and Python. scripts/run_all.sh builds the Lean project, checks the axioms and runs the checks.

title: Técnicas para el modelado y la generación de audio en trastornos del habla : evaluación comparativa de tecnologías de generación de voz para la síntesis de habla con disartria.
abstract: En la actualidad, el crecimiento acelerado de la inteligencia artificial ha abierto nuevos caminos para el procesamiento y generación de audios que imitan la voz. Sin embargo, para la disartria, estos nuevos horizontes enfrentan un imponente desafío: la escasez de datos para el entrenamiento y evaluación de modelos de vanguardia. Las personas con disartria presentan alteraciones motoras del habla, lo que puede afectar la inteligibilidad, la prosodia y la calidad acústica de la voz; esto provoca una limitación al desarrollar tecnologías orientadas a esta patología. Bajo este enfoque, se propone la evaluación comparativa de tecnologías de generación y conversión de voz para la creación de datos sintéticos del habla disártrica. En el capítulo 1 se presenta el problema, los objetivos, el alcance y el marco teórico relacionado con disartria, tecnologías generativas, conversión de voz y métricas objetivas. En el Capítulo 2 se describe la metodología, incluyendo el uso del dataset TORGO, los procesos de limpieza, normalización, extracción de representaciones acústicas y ejecución de los modelos seleccionados. En el Capítulo 3 se presentan los resultados de la comparación entre enfoques basados en redes generativas, modelos secuenciales y modelos de difusión, evaluados mediante métricas objetivas de inteligibilidad, calidad acústica y similitud espectral. Finalmente, se exponen las conclusiones y recomendaciones orientadas a identificar qué tecnologías presentan mejores condiciones técnicas para futuras estrategias de aumento de datos sintéticos en datasets disártricos.

Las personas con disartria presentan alteraciones motoras del habla, lo que puede afectar la inteligibilidad, la prosodia y la calidad acústica de la voz; esto provoca una limitación al desarrollar tecnologías orientadas a esta patología. Bajo este enfoque, se propone la evaluación comparativa de tecnologías de generación y conversión de voz para la creación de datos sintéticos del habla disártrica. En el capítulo 1 se presenta el problema, los objetivos, el alcance y el marco teórico relacionado con disartria, tecnologías generativas, conversión de voz y métricas objetivas. En el Capítulo 2 se describe la metodología, incluyendo el uso del dataset TORGO, los procesos de limpieza, normalización, extracción de representaciones acústicas y ejecución de los modelos seleccionados. En el Capítulo 3 se presentan los resultados de la comparación entre enfoques basados en redes generativas, modelos secuenciales y modelos de difusión, evaluados mediante métricas objetivas de inteligibilidad, calidad acústica y similitud espectral. Finalmente, se exponen las conclusiones y recomendaciones orientadas a identificar qué tecnologías presentan mejores condiciones técnicas para futuras estrategias de aumento de datos sintéticos en datasets disártricos.

title: Classificação automática de sentenças faladas com arquitetura híbrida: análise de estruturas topicalizadas, anti-topicalizadas e canônicas
abstract: O presente artigo investiga o desempenho de um sistema de classificação automática de sentenças faladas do português brasileiro, considerando estruturas canônicas, topicalizadas e antitopicalizadas, por meio de uma arquitetura híbrida baseada em Redes Neurais Recorrentes (RNNs) e Redes Neurais Convolucionais (CNNs). A pesquisa articula contribuições sintáticas, prosódicas e computacionais com a finalidade de contextualizar o corpus e delimitar o tratamento das sentenças faladas, porém o estudo concentra-se na avaliação experimental de uma arquitetura híbrida de redes neurais aplicada à classificação automática dessas sentenças. O corpus analisado é composto por 612 sentenças declarativas gravadas em ambiente controlado, produzidas por 20 falantes do português brasileiro. A metodologia caracteriza-se como quantitativa e experimental, utilizando aprendizagem supervisionada e avaliação baseada em métricas como precisão, recall, f-score e acurácia, por meio da matriz de confusão. Foram realizados testes com diferentes configurações de hiperparâmetros, variando filtros convolucionais, unidades LSTM, taxas de Dropout e número de épocas de treinamento. Os resultados demonstraram que modelos mais robustos apresentaram maior capacidade de memorização dos dados de treino, mas também maior tendência ao overfitting. Em contrapartida, arquiteturas mais enxutas associadas a maiores taxas de regularização obtiveram melhor capacidade de generalização e maior estabilidade durante a validação. O melhor desempenho foi observado no cenário com 30% de Dropout, em que houve redução significativa do hiato de generalização entre treino e teste. Conclui-se que a combinação entre RNNs e CNNs mostra-se promissora para a classificação automática de sentenças faladas, embora ainda existam limitações relacionadas à generalização do modelo em dados não vistos.

title: A Brazilian Dataset for Financial Sentiment Analysis: An Active Learning-Based Annotation Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a new expert-annotated dataset for financial sentiment analysis in Brazilian Portuguese, constructed from earnings call transcripts of the banking sector. The dataset was developed using a two-stage active learning pipeline designed to reduce annotation cost while preserving data quality. In the first stage, clustering and active learning were combined to filter relevant sentences from noisy transcripts. In the second stage, a Query by Committee strategy combining the transformer models BERTimbau and DeB3RTa was employed to select informative samples for expert annotation. The resulting dataset contains 719 annotated sentences with agreement analysis across multiple annotators. We further evaluated BERTimbau, DeB3RTa, and the external transformer model BERTuguês under three experimental settings, including fine-grained eight-class classification and complementary three-class scenarios. In the eight-class setting, BERTuguês and BERTimbau achieved comparable F1-macro scores (0.43±0.03 and 0.43 ± 0.01, respectively). In the sentiment-only three-class setup, BERTimbau achieved the best performance (0.68± 0.06). These results suggest that the dataset supports both fine-grained and coarse-grained sentiment analysis while remaining useful for models not involved in the active learning process.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Individual Planning and Collaborative Planning in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems must frequently balance individual autonomy against collaborative coordination when solving complex tasks in dynamic environments. Individual planning allows each agent to generate and execute plans using its own observations, objectives, computational resources, and local knowledge. Collaborative planning enables multiple agents to exchange information, resolve dependencies, negotiate shared decisions, and construct mutually compatible plans. However, neither planning mode is universally optimal. Continuous collaboration can introduce communication overhead, coordination delays, computational costs, and unnecessary information exchange, whereas exclusive reliance on individual planning can result in incompatible plans, duplicated work, missed dependencies, and avoidable failures. This paper proposes an adaptive planning framework that dynamically switches between individual planning and collaborative planning according to the estimated benefits and costs of coordination. The framework introduces a planning-mode controller that evaluates task dependencies, uncertainty, predicted plan conflicts, expected performance improvement, resource availability, and communication overhead. It supports transitions between individual planning, collaborative planning, and intermediate coordination states without requiring the system to follow a permanently fixed planning strategy. The proposed framework is formalized as a sequential decision problem and incorporates a switching-cost mechanism to prevent unstable mode changes. An evaluation methodology is developed to compare the framework against permanently individual, permanently collaborative, periodic-switching, and non-adaptive hybrid baselines. This work establishes a research direction for cost-aware, context-sensitive planning in multi-agent systems. The framework is presented as a methodological proposal; its comparative advantages remain to be established through empirical evaluation.

title: BEYOND AUTOMATION: INVESTIGATING THE INFLUENCE OF COGNITIVE BIASES ON HUMAN INTERPRETATION OF EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: BEYOND AUTOMATION: INVESTIGATING THE INFLUENCE OF COGNITIVE BIASES ON HUMAN INTERPRETATION OF EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE PROF(DR.) VIJAYKUMAR B GADHAVI PROFESSOR AND HEAD , SWARRNIM INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, SWARRNIM START-UP AND INNOVATION UNIVERSITY - GANDHINAGAR GUJARAT INDIA ORCID: 0009-0005-6313-5900, E-MAIL: DRVIJAYKUMAR@SWARRNIM.EDU.IN PARMAR JIGAR JAYSUKHBHAI B. TECH. CE STUDENT, SWARRNIM INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY SWARRNIM STARTUP & INNOVATION UNIVERSITY, GANDHINAGAR, GUJARAT, INDIA ORCID: 0009-0008-7651-9913, EMAIL: JIGARAHIR410@GMAIL.COM Abstract Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is intended to make algorithmic outputs more understandable, auditable, and contestable. Yet an explanation does not reach a neutral observer: people interpret it through prior beliefs, cognitive shortcuts, professional experience, and assumptions about machine competence. This conceptual paper examines how cognitive biases shape the interpretation of XAI and why greater transparency does not necessarily produce better decisions. Drawing on research on automation bias, judgment and decision-making, explainability, and human–AI collaboration, the paper develops an integrative framework linking explanation characteristics, user cognition, task context, and reliance behavior. It argues that anchoring, confirmation bias, availability, authority effects, and cognitive miserliness can transform explanations into persuasive cues rather than evidence for independent evaluation. Explanations may improve mental models and error detection when they are faithful, appropriately scoped, and matched to users’ needs; however, they may also legitimize an incorrect prediction, increase cognitive load, or create an illusion of understanding. The paper proposes design principles centered on calibrated trust, contrastive and uncertainty-aware explanations, independent judgment, verification prompts, and evaluation of decision quality rather than satisfaction alone. Because this is a conceptual synthesis rather than an empirical study, its propositions require experimental testing across domains and user groups. The central conclusion is that responsible XAI must design not only for model transparency but also for the cognitive conditions under which people interpret explanations. Keywords: explainable artificial intelligence, cognitive bias, automation bias, human–AI interaction, trust calibration, decision-making, algorithmic transparency

title: Looped Language Models: A Survey and Meta-Analysis of Recurrent-Depth Transformers
abstract: Looped language models apply one shared block of Transformer layers repeatedly to the same tokens. Their effective depth, the number of layer applications per token, can grow without adding parameters and can be chosen at inference time. Recurrent depth is thus a way to scale test-time compute in latent space instead of in generated tokens. The idea appears under many names, including looped Transformers, LoopLMs, recurrent-depth models, Universal Transformers, Mixture-of-Recursions, and recursive reasoning models such as HRM and TRM. In two years it has moved from synthetic tasks to open models such as Huginn and Ouro and to pretraining on up to 28 trillion tokens. According to press reports, it is also used in a frontier-lab model. Its literature has split across architecture, training, systems, theory and safety. We present the first survey dedicated to looped language models, built on a systematic corpus of 557 core papers screened from 7,323 candidates. We introduce a unified prelude–core–coda formalism that makes explicit how parameters, compute, memory and depth are counted. We organize the field from design, training and scaling to inference systems, theory, mechanisms, capabilities, other modalities and safety. A meta-analysis classifies 822 verified empirical claims by comparison regime. It shows that most apparent contradictions about whether “a recurrence is worth a layer” come from comparing parameter-matched with compute-matched results. The evidence fits one reading, in which a recurrence is worth less than a fresh block of parameters. Looping therefore helps when parameters are the limiting resource and hurts when it replaces them at fixed compute. We derive a research agenda from measured gaps, including the absence of work on robustness, alignment and privacy. We release the corpus, the extraction records with verbatim evidence for every number, and the claims ledger.

title: Version 6.9.24 - AI-KM: Agent Preset, Agent Swarm, and Agent Scaffold
abstract: The integration of agent technologies and knowledge management has progressed from conversational question answering toward composable AI capabilities. However, existing systems still exhibit three common gaps: agent definitions are difficult to capture as portable assets, multi-agent collaboration lacks organizational mechanisms with low cognitive overhead, and large-scale agent workloads over real-world operational data lack a unified execution foundation. This update to AI-KM addresses these gaps through three capabilities: Agent Preset, Agent Swarm, and Agent Scaffold. Agent Preset packages roles, models, capability boundaries, skills, and private knowledge into declarative, distributable, and versionable agent assets, with capability boundaries enforced by the runtime rather than by prompts. Agent Swarm organizes multiple presets into a single natural-language collaboration, replacing structured blackboards and event protocols with group-chat history injection and flexible @mention-based invocation, thereby making multi-agent collaboration a first-class interaction mode within the conversational interface. Agent Scaffold organizes execution configurations into an orthogonal configuration space and introduces multi-round execution and fingerprint-based incremental change detection. The three capabilities share the same execution engine, capability model, and message model, thereby maintaining behavioral consistency while forming an integrated workflow for creating, organizing, and operating agents at scale.

title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
abstract: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.
